Lily and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump and slide. They saw a big tree with a hole. They wanted to see what was inside.

They went to the tree and looked in the hole. They saw a big owl with yellow eyes. The owl was sleeping. Lily and Ben were curious. They wanted to say hello to the owl.

"Hello, owl!" Lily said in a loud voice. She waved her hand at the owl.

The owl woke up. He was not happy. He did not like to be disturbed. He made a loud noise. He flapped his wings. He looked angry.

"Go away, go away!" the owl said. He glared at Lily and Ben.

Lily and Ben were scared. They ran away from the tree. They did not want to make the owl more angry.

They felt ashamed. They knew they should not have bothered the owl. They should have let him sleep.

They went to their mom. They told her what happened. Their mom hugged them. She said they should be more careful and respectful of animals.

She said they could say sorry to the owl later, when he was awake and calm. She said maybe the owl would be friendly then.

Lily and Ben nodded. They learned their lesson. They hoped the owl would forgive them.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys. Today, they have a new game. They pretend to be in a restaurant. Anna is the cook and Ben is the customer.

Ben sits at the table and looks at the menu. He sees many things he likes. He wants to order pizza, ice cream, and juice. He says to Anna, "I want pizza, ice cream, and juice, please."

Anna shakes her head. She says, "No, you cannot have pizza, ice cream, and juice. That is too much. You have to choose one thing."

Ben is not happy. He says, "But I want all of them. They are yummy. You are a bad cook. You have to give me what I want."

Anna is angry. She says, "No, I am a good cook. You are a bad customer. You have to follow the rules. You can only have one thing. Or you can have nothing."

Ben thinks for a moment. He does not want to have nothing. He likes to eat. He looks at the menu again. He sees something he does not like. He sees black. He does not like black. He says to Anna, "OK, I will choose one thing. I will have black, please."

Anna is surprised. She says, "Black? You want black? Why do you want black? Black is not food. Black is a color. You cannot eat black."

Ben smiles. He says, "I know. I do not want to eat black. I want to trick you. I want to make you excited. I want to see your face when you try to give me black."

Anna is not amused. She says, "That is not funny. That is silly. You are a silly customer. You do not know how to play. I do not want to play with you anymore."

She takes the menu and the toys and goes to her room. Ben is left alone at the table. He feels sad. He says to himself, "Maybe I was too silly. Maybe I should say sorry to Anna. Maybe we can play again."

One day, Ben and Lily went to the park with their mom. They saw a big pond with ducks and fish. They wanted to feed the ducks some bread. Mom gave them some bread and said, "Be careful, don't go too close to the water."

Ben and Lily threw some bread to the ducks. The ducks were happy and quacked. But then, they saw something else in the water. It was an alligator! It had big teeth and a long tail. It looked hungry and angry. It swam towards the ducks and the bread.

"Look, mom, an alligator!" Ben shouted.

"Oh no, it's going to eat the ducks!" Lily cried.

Mom grabbed Ben and Lily and pulled them away from the pond. She said, "Stay here, I'll call for help."

But Ben and Lily didn't want to leave the ducks. They wanted to save them from the alligator. They saw a big stick on the ground. They picked it up and ran back to the pond. They waved the stick at the alligator and shouted, "Go away, go away, you filthy alligator!"

The alligator was surprised and scared. It didn't like the stick and the noise. It turned around and swam away from the pond. The ducks were safe and thanked Ben and Lily with more quacks.

Mom came back with a park ranger. She saw Ben and Lily with the stick and the ducks. She was proud and relieved. She hugged them and said, "You are very brave, but also very naughty. You shouldn't go near the alligator. It could have hurt you."

Ben and Lily said, "We're sorry, mom. We just wanted to save the ducks. They are our friends."

Mom said, "I know, but you have to be careful. Alligators are dangerous and filthy. They don't belong in the pond. The park ranger will take it away and put it in a better place."

Ben and Lily nodded and said, "Okay, mom. We love you."

They gave the ducks some more bread and said goodbye. They left the park with mom and the park ranger. They were happy and proud. They had saved the ducks from the alligator.

One day, she found a strange bottle in her mom's closet. It had a label that said "Shrink". Lila was curious and opened the bottle. She smelled a sweet scent and felt a tickle in her nose. She sneezed and dropped the bottle.

"Oh no!" she said. She looked around and saw that everything was huge. The bottle, the sheet, the dolls, the bed, the door. She had shrunk to the size of a mouse.

She heard her mom calling her name. "Lila, where are you? It's time for lunch!"

Lila was scared and tried to find a way out. She climbed on the sheet and saw a hole in the corner. She crawled through the hole and saw a bright light. She followed the light and came out under the bed.

She saw her mom's feet walking towards the door. She ran after her and shouted. "Mom, mom, help me! I'm here! I'm tiny!"

Her mom heard a faint voice and looked down. She saw Lila waving at her. She was shocked and picked her up. "Lila, what happened to you? How did you shrink?"

Lila told her mom about the bottle and the sneeze. Her mom hugged her and said. "Don't worry, sweetie. I know how to fix this. I have another bottle that says "Grow". Come on, let's go to the bathroom and make you big again."

Lila was happy and relieved. She thanked her mom and said. "I'm sorry, mom. I won't touch your things again. I learned my lesson. Shrink is a bad word."

Her mom smiled and said. "It's okay, Lila. I love you. And you're right. Shrink is a bad word. But you know what's a good word? Sheet. You can still play with your sheet and your dolls. They're waiting for you in your room."

Lila nodded and said. "Yes, mom. I love you too. And I love my sheet and my dolls. They're my friends. But I'm not shy anymore. I'm brave. I can face anything. Even shrink."

The thin rope thought for a moment. It was a very tricky situation because the knot was so tight. It then had an idea. If it kept rocking back and forth, it could slowly move the knot and release the mouse. 

The rope worked hard. For several days and nights it would rock back and forth, slowly moving the knot and helping the mouse. Finally, one day, the knot was loose enough for the mouse to escape! The thin rope was so happy that it got its reward. The mouse gave it a big hug, thanked it and ran off.

The thin rope learned an important lesson that day - never give up and be kind to everyone, no matter how helpless they may seem. All it takes is a bit of effort and you can help make a difference!

Once upon a time there was a boy named John. He was very small, only three-years-old. Everyday he liked to take naps and lay on the desk.

One day, John was feeling very sleepy. He wanted to lay on the desk, but it was covered with lots of toys. He wanted to play but he was so sleepy. He felt so frustrated he could not lay on the desk.

John felt like he was missing out on something, but he didn't know what. He decided to try to find a new place to lay and take a nap. He got up and began to run very fast around the house.

At last, he found the perfect spot - a comfy one-seater couch. John felt relieved to have a place to lay and take a nap. Just then, he realized that he never noticed the comfy couch before. That's when he realized that he could lay on the couch instead of the desk!

John was glad he found a new place to lay and take a nap. From now on, whenever John felt sleepy, he knew he could lay on the couch. He felt happy and relaxed, knowing that he had a cozy place to rest his head.

Mummy was very sorry. She knew she had to collect every bit of the poison, and put it in her big bag. So she made a circle with the stick, and all of the poison was inside the circle.

Then Mummy put all the poison in her bag and went home. She was very sorry for what had happened, but at least she had kept the little ones safe.

Once upon a time there was an old house that had lots of stairs. In the house was a little girl who was only three years old.

The little girl said, "I like to match the blocks. What do you like to do?"

Suddenly the old house creaked and an old voice said, "I like to climb up and down the stairs." 

The little girl hopped off the blocks and ran up and down the stairs. She went up and down, up and down until she was out of breath.

The little girl said, "I matched the blocks and now I am going to match the stairs! There are so many stairs to climb. Which stair shall I climb first?" 

The old house creaked and the old voice said, "Climb the top stair. It's the tallest!"

So the little girl began to climb the stairs, matching each stair until she reached the top. 

When she stepped off the top stair she said, "I matched the blocks, I matched the stairs, and now I'm at the top! What an adventure!"

Once upon a time, a little girl called Joy was playing in the park. Suddenly, she heard a loud siren. She peeked out of the bushes and saw an ambulance. All of the grown-ups were running away, so Joy felt scared. 

Suddenly, a hairy dog came running up to Joy. The dog barked loudly! Joy said, "What is it, doggy? Is something wrong?" 

The doggy kept running and barking, and led Joy to where the ambulance was. Joy found out that a little boy had fallen down, and he was hurt. Joy called out to the ambulance, and the driver stopped to help the boy. 

The driver smiled at Joy and said, "Thanks for peeking around, little girl. You saved the day!" Everyone was very happy, and the little boy was okay. The hairy dog even licked Joy's face, to say a big thank you. 

Joy and the doggy happily walked back to the park, and Joy was proud of her brave act. She knew she had made the world a better place. 
The End.

Once upon a time there was an enormous diamond in the forest. It glistened brightly in the sunshine and all the animals could see it from a mile away. One day a little rabbit hopped up to the diamond and said, "I am going to take this diamond and leave my burrow forever." 

Just as she was about to take the diamond, a big rabbit hopped out from behind a tree and said, "No! You must never leave. We need you here to take care of us." 

The little rabbit was so sad; she wanted to take the diamond more than anything else. Suddenly a low rumble filled the air and the ground began shaking. The big rabbit said, "Quick! We must leave now!" 

The little rabbit picked up the diamond and ran as fast as she could, following the big rabbit through the woods. The ground was shaking so much that she almost dropped the diamond, but she held it tightly. After what felt like hours, they finally arrived at a safe place. 

The big rabbit said, "I knew the ground would start shaking like that. I knew you wouldn't be able to leave with the diamond." The little rabbit was so relieved to have the diamond and to be safe. The big rabbit had saved her, and she was glad to stay in her burrow after all.

The man smiled and waved back. He asked Johnnie to come closer, and Johnnie smiled. The two of them talked for a few minutes, and then the man blinked very slowly. He produced a handful of candy from his pocket and offered it to Johnnie.

Johnnie reached out to take the candy, but the elderly man said, "Remember, if something looks too good to be true, it probably is." He winked at Johnnie and then walked away.

Johnnie's heart sank. He looked at the candy that the man had left behind and realized it was made of fondant, not chocolate. He had been tricked! He put the candy back on the bench and ran home, making sure to be more careful in the future.

The moral of the story is that you should never trust someone too quickly, especially if something looks too good to be true. Always listen to your elders and be careful when accepting gifts from strangers.

Slowly, he stepped forward, looking curiously at the magical dance. He wanted to join the other animals, the way they jumped and twirled and moved around. He wanted to dance too.

But when Bobby tried to join them, he was so clumsy and out of place and all the other animals started laughing. Still, he persisted, but he stumbled upon his feet and made the other animals laugh even more.

Feeling embarrassed and sad, Bobby slowly slunk away and disappeared into the woods, never to dance again.

"Well, my doll has a nose. And she can wipe it when she is sick. She is very wise. She knows how to take care of herself." Lily said, hugging her doll.

Tom stopped laughing. He remembered that he had a cold and his nose was runny. He looked for a tissue, but he couldn't find any. He felt a drop of snot on his lip. He felt embarrassed and gross.

"Lily, can I borrow your tissue?" Tom asked, in a small voice.

"Sure, Tom. Here you go. You should wipe your nose when it is runny. It will make you feel better." Lily said, handing him her tissue.

"Thank you, Lily. You are very kind. And you are right. Your doll is very wise. She knows how to take care of herself. And so do you." Tom said, wiping his nose and smiling.

"You're welcome, Tom. And you are very smart. You know how to play with your truck and make fun noises and lights. And you know how to say sorry and thank you." Lily said, smiling back.

Tom and Lily hugged each other and continued to play with their toys. They learned to share and appreciate each other's toys. They also learned to wipe their noses when they were sick. They were happy and healthy friends.

The moral value of the story is: be kind and respectful to others, and take care of yourself.

Bun-Bun wanted to help his friend, so he started to look around. After a few minutes, he found a shiny acorn on the ground. But when Nutty came to see it, Bun-Bun realized it was a fake one! They both laughed and continued to search for the real acorn.

From that day on, Bun-Bun learned to be careful when jumping into piles of leaves, and he and Nutty became even better friends.

Sara loved to read books. She had many books in her room, but her favorite one was the purple book. The purple book had pictures of animals and their names. Sara liked to learn new words and say them out loud.

One day, Sara wanted to read the purple book to her little brother, Tom. She went to her room and looked for the book on her shelf. But she could not find it. She looked under her bed, in her closet, and in her toy box. But the purple book was not there.

"Where is my purple book?" Sara asked herself. She felt sad and angry. She thought maybe Tom took it. She went to his room and knocked on the door.

"Tom, do you have my purple book?" Sara asked.

"No, I don't," Tom said. "Why do you want it?"

"Because it is my favorite book and I want to read it to you," Sara said.

"Well, I don't want to hear it. I have my own book," Tom said. He showed Sara his book. It was a red book with pictures of cars and trucks. Tom liked to make noises and pretend to drive them.

"That book is not impressive," Sara said. "The purple book is better. It has animals and words."

"That book is boring," Tom said. "The red book is more fun. It has sounds and wheels."

Sara and Tom started to argue. They both thought their book was the best. They raised their voices and said mean things to each other.

Their mom heard them and came to see what was wrong. She saw them holding their books and frowning.

"What is going on here?" she asked.

"Sara wants my book and I don't want to give it to her," Tom said.

"Tom has my book and he won't let me read it to him," Sara said.

Mom looked at the books and smiled. She had an idea.

"Why don't you try to share your books?" she suggested. "Maybe you can learn something new from each other. Sara, you can show Tom the animals and their names. Tom, you can show Sara the cars and trucks and their sounds. You might find out that both books are impressive in their own way."

Sara and Tom looked at each other. They felt a little sorry for being rude. They decided to give mom's idea a try. They sat down on the floor and opened their books. They took turns reading and listening. They learned some new words and noises. They also laughed and had fun.

They realized that mom was right. Both books were impressive. And so were they.

"Sorry, Mom, we were having fun. We didn't mean to," Ben says.

"OK, Mom, thank you. We love you," Sara and Ben say.

They go to the bathroom and take a bath. Mom rubs them with a towel and makes them dry. Then they have lunch together. They are happy.

The moral of the story is: Listen to your mom and don't play in the puddle.

The lion did not understand what that meant until the squirrels explained it to him. A broken story means that parts of the story have been forgotten.

The lion did not give up and he set off on a journey to find the missing parts of his story. Along the way, he heard his roar again and again. Eventually, he found all of the missing pieces. 

Once he put them together, his story was complete. His roar was just as loud as before and everyone in the forest was so happy. The lion was happy too and he roared out loud so that everyone in the forest could hear.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Lily cried. "Bad chicken! Why did you bite me?"

"What happened, sweetie?" Mommy asked.

"Mommy, the chicken bit me!" Lily sobbed. "It hurt me!"

Mommy looked at the chicken. It was still adorable, but it had a naughty smile on its beak. Mommy realized that the chicken was not a real chicken, but a toy chicken that made noises when you squeezed it. She guessed that Lily had squeezed it too hard and triggered the bite sound.

"Sweetie, the chicken did not really bite you. It was just a toy sound. See?" Mommy said. She squeezed the chicken gently and it made a cluck sound. "It's just a silly chicken. It did not mean to hurt you."

Lily looked at the chicken and then at Mommy. She sniffed and wiped her tears. She felt better. She smiled and said, "Oh, I see. It's just a silly chicken. I'm sorry, chicken. I did not mean to squeeze you."

Lily nodded and said, "Yes, please. But not this chicken. This chicken is my friend."

"Stop!" Mom says. She comes into the living room. She sees the mess. She sees the broken vase, the broken lamp, and the angry cat. She sees Jill and Ben in the old clothes. She is not happy.

"What are you doing?" Mom asks.

"We are dancing," Jill and Ben say.

"Well, your dance is over," Mom says. "You have to clean up this mess. And you have to put back the old things. They are not yours. They are Grandma's. She gave them to me. They are very special."

Jill and Ben feel bad. They did not know. They say sorry to Mom. They say sorry to the cat. They take off the old clothes. They help Mom clean up the mess. They put back the old things in the box. They do not dance anymore. They are quiet and sad.

Mom sees them. She hugs them. She says, "I know you like to dance. And I like to see you happy. But you have to be careful. You have to respect other people's things. And you have to watch where you are going. Do you understand?"

Jill and Ben nod. They understand. They say sorry again. They say they love Mom. They say they love Grandma. They say they love the old things.

Mom smiles. She says, "I love you too. And I love Grandma. And I love the old things. But you know what? I also love to dance. Do you want to dance with me?"

Jill and Ben smile. They say yes. They hug Mom. They turn on the music. They dance and dance. But this time, they are careful. They do not break anything. They do not hurt anyone. They are happy. And so is Mom. And so is the cat. And so is Grandma, who is watching them from a picture on the wall.

Tom and Anna shook their heads. They did not like vegetables. They only liked candy and cake.

Mom was sad. She wanted them to eat healthy food. She had an idea. She cut the zucchini into small pieces and mixed them with cheese and eggs. She baked them in the oven and made zucchini muffins.

"Look, I made some yummy muffins for you. Do you want to try some?" she asked.

Tom and Anna smelled the muffins and their mouths watered. They liked muffins. They took a bite and smiled. They did not know there was zucchini inside. They liked the muffins very much.

"Mom, these are the best muffins ever! Can we have more?" they asked.

Mom was happy. She hugged them and said, "Of course, you can have more. But you have to promise me something. Next time you see a new vegetable, do not panic. Do not be scared. Try it and you might like it. Vegetables are good for you. They make you strong and smart."

Tom and Anna nodded. They learned a lesson. They decided to try new vegetables and not judge them by their looks. They thanked mom for the muffins and the lesson. They ate the muffins and felt good. They were not scared of zucchini anymore. They were brave and curious.

Tim and Lily were clumsy and naughty. They did not listen to their mother. They went to the truck and played with the shiny things. They caused a fire and a boom. They died in the truck. They did not have a happy ending.

Lily and Ben were friends. They liked to play with toys and books. One day, they found a big mug in the kitchen. It was blue and had a picture of a cat on it. Lily and Ben both wanted the mug.

"Give me the mug!" Lily said. "It is mine!"

"No, it is mine!" Ben said. "I saw it first!"

They pulled and pushed the mug. They did not share. They were ignorant. They did not know how to be nice.

The mug broke. It fell on the floor and made a loud noise. Lily and Ben were sad. They cried. They had no mug and no fun.

Mom came and saw the mess. She was angry. She scolded Lily and Ben. She told them to say sorry and to share. She told them to be kind and not ignorant.

Lily and Ben felt bad. They said sorry to each other. They hugged. They learned a lesson. They decided to share their toys and books. They were friends again. They had fun.

Tom and Lily liked to play with their toys in the living room. They had a lot of fun making noises and pretending to be animals. One day, they found a big box with a record player and some records inside. They wanted to try it out and see what it sounded like.

"Let's play this one!" Tom said, picking up a record with a picture of a lion on it. He put it on the record player and turned it on. The record player made a loud roar and a music.

"Wow, that's cool!" Lily said, clapping her hands. "Can I try another one?"

"Sure, but be careful. Don't scratch the records. They are old and fragile," Tom said, handing her another record with a picture of a bird on it.

Lily took the record and put it on the record player. She turned it on and heard a sweet song and a chirp. She smiled and danced along.

"This one is nice!" she said. "Can I keep it?"

"No, you can't. It's not yours. It's Mom's. She loves these records. She said they are very special to her," Tom said, taking the record from her.

"But I like it too! I want it!" Lily said, pulling the record back.

"Stop it! You'll break it!" Tom said, pulling harder.

They both tugged and fought over the record, not listening to each other. The record slipped from their hands and fell on the floor. It cracked and split in two.

They both gasped and looked at the broken record. They heard Mom coming into the living room.

"What's going on here?" Mom asked, seeing the mess. She saw the record player and the records. She saw the broken record with the bird on it. She picked it up and felt a tear in her eye.

"This was my favorite record. It was a gift from Grandma. She used to sing this song to me when I was little. How could you do this?" Mom asked, looking at Tom and Lily with a sad and angry face.

Tom and Lily felt very bad. They knew they had done something wrong. They wished they had been calm and shared the record. They wished they had not fought over it. They wished they had not broken it.

They said they were sorry, but Mom was still upset. She said they had to go to their rooms and think about what they had done. She said they had to stay there until dinner. She said they had to help her fix the record later.

She took the record and the record player and put them in the box. She wrapped the box with a rag and put it away. She hoped she could glue the record back together, but she knew it would never sound the same.

Tom and Lily went to their rooms, feeling sad and guilty. They learned a hard lesson that day. They learned that they should respect other people's things. They learned that they should not fight over things that are not theirs. They learned that they should be calm and share with each other. They learned that some things are precious and can't be replaced.

Ben was a lazy boy. He did not like to help his mom and dad with the chores. He only liked to play with his toys and watch TV. He did not listen when his mom and dad told him to tidy his room, wash his hands, or eat his vegetables.

One day, Ben saw a big hole in the hedge. He was curious and wanted to see what was on the other side. He did not listen when his mom and dad told him to stay away from the hedge. He crawled through the hole and found himself in a strange garden. He saw many flowers, fruits, and animals. He thought it was a fun place to play.

But he did not know that the garden belonged to a mean witch. The witch did not like children who were lazy and did not listen. She saw Ben and decided to teach him a lesson. She waved her wand and turned him into a snail. She said, "Now you will have to work hard to move around and find food. And you will have to listen to me or I will step on you."

Ben was scared and sorry. He wished he had listened to his mom and dad and stayed away from the hedge. He did not like being a snail. He wanted to go back to his home and his toys and his TV. He hoped the witch would change him back.

He saw a friendly bird in the garden. He asked the bird for help. The bird said, "I can help you, but you have to promise me something. You have to promise to be a good boy and not be lazy and listen to your mom and dad. Do you promise?" Ben said, "Yes, I promise. Please help me." The bird said, "OK, follow me." The bird flew to the hole in the hedge and showed Ben the way. Ben crawled as fast as he could. He was happy to see his home again.

The witch saw Ben escaping and was angry. She tried to catch him, but the bird pecked her nose and made her drop her wand. The wand hit the ground and broke. The spell was broken too. Ben turned back into a boy. He ran to his mom and dad and hugged them. He said, "I'm sorry I was lazy and did not listen. I love you and I will be a good boy from now on." His mom and dad were glad and forgave him. They said, "We love you too, Ben. We are proud of you for learning your lesson."

The moral of the story is: Be a good boy and not be lazy and listen to your mom and dad. They know what is best for you and they want you to be happy and safe.

Tim and Kim are twins. They like to play outside. They have a red cap and a blue cap. They take turns to wear the caps.

One day, they go to the park with Mom. Mom says, "Stay close to me. The park is big and there are many people. Do not get lost." Tim and Kim nod. They hold Mom's hand.

They see a big slide. They want to go on the slide. Mom says, "OK, but be careful. Do not push or run. Wait for your turn." Tim and Kim nod. They let go of Mom's hand.

Tim wears the red cap. He goes first. He climbs up the ladder. He sits on the slide. He says, "Whee!" He slides down. He laughs. He feels happy.

Kim wears the blue cap. She goes next. She climbs up the ladder. She sits on the slide. She says, "Whee!" She slides down. She screams. She feels scared.

A big dog is at the bottom of the slide. The dog sees the blue cap. The dog thinks it is a toy. The dog jumps and bites the blue cap. The dog pulls the blue cap off Kim's head. The dog runs away with the blue cap.

Kim cries. She says, "My cap! My cap! The dog took my cap!" She looks for Mom. She does not see Mom. She sees many people. She does not know them. She feels lost.

Tim hears Kim cry. He runs to Kim. He says, "Don't cry, Kim. I am here. We will find Mom. We will get your cap back." He hugs Kim. He looks for Mom. He does not see Mom. He sees many people. He does not know them. He feels lost.

Mom hears Tim and Kim cry. She runs to Tim and Kim. She says, "Oh, my babies! I am here. I am sorry. I lost sight of you. Are you OK?" She hugs Tim and Kim. She sees the dog with the blue cap. She says, "Oh, no! The dog took your cap! I am sorry. I will buy you a new cap." She takes Tim and Kim's hand.

They go to the exit. They see a sign. The sign says, "Beware of the dog. The dog is not safe. The dog bites." Mom says, "Oh, no! We should have read the sign. We should have stayed away from the slide. We should have been more careful." She feels sad.

They leave the park. They spend the rest of the day at home. They do not play outside. They do not laugh. They do not feel happy. They have a bad day.

"Are you OK?" he asked. "That was a bad snake. It could have bitten you."

"Thank you, mister," Ben said. "You saved our ball and us."

"Thank you, thank you," Lily said. "You are very brave and kind."

The man smiled and patted their heads. "You're welcome, kids. But be careful next time. Don't play near snakes. They like the heat and the grass. And always stay alert and watch where you go."

Ben and Lily nodded. They hugged their ball and thanked the man again. Then they ran to their mom, who was waiting for them at the bench. They told her what happened and how the man helped them. She was glad they were safe and gave them some water and cookies. They ate and drank and felt better. They decided to play with their ball in a different place, away from the snake. They had fun and learned a lesson.

"Tom, don't be sad. We are going to a new house. It will be nice and cozy. You will have a new sofa to sleep on. And you will have a new friend. A little dog. He is very friendly and playful. He will make you happy." his owner says.

"Meow, meow, meow!" Tom says. He does not want a new friend. He does not like dogs. He thinks they are loud and annoying. He does not want to be happy. He only wants to sleep.

"Tom, please trust me. It will be okay. I love you very much. Now, come on. Let's go to the truck. We have to go now." his owner says.

She picks up Tom and puts him in a cage. She carries him to the truck. Tom does not like the cage. He does not like the truck. He does not like the new house. He does not like the new friend. He does not like anything.

He closes his eyes and tries to sleep. He hopes it is all a bad dream. He hopes he will wake up on his old sofa. He hopes he will be alone and quiet. He hopes he will be happy.

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play in their big wardrobe. They had many clothes and toys inside, and they pretended to be different people and animals. Sometimes they were pirates, sometimes they were fairies, sometimes they were lions.

One day, they decided to be lazy and stay in the wardrobe all day. They made a cozy nest with blankets and pillows, and they read books and ate snacks. They enjoyed being lazy very much.

"Tom, do you want to play a game?" Lily asked.

"Maybe later, Lily. I want to finish this book. It is very good," Tom said.

"What is it about?" Lily asked.

"It is about a boy who goes to a magic land inside a wardrobe. He meets a lion and a witch and a faun," Tom said.

"That sounds fun. Can I read it too?" Lily asked.

"Sure, Lily. Here you go," Tom said, and gave her the book.

They both read the book and imagined they were in the magic land. They forgot about the time and the outside world. They were happy and lazy in their wardrobe.

Lily and Tom were very excited to see the comet. Mom said it was a big ball of ice and dust that flew in the sky. She said it was very rare and special. She said they had to stay up late to see it.

But when it was time to go outside, it started to rain. Lily and Tom were sad. They wanted to see the comet, not the rain. Mom said they had to wait a little bit. She said the rain would stop soon and the sky would be clear. She said the comet would not go away. She said it was delayed.

"What does delayed mean?" Lily asked.

"It means it takes longer to come," Mom said. "But it will come, don't worry."

Lily and Tom waited and waited. They played with their toys and read their books. They looked out the window and saw the rain stop. They saw the stars come out. They saw the moon shine.

"Can we go outside now?" Tom asked.

"Yes, we can," Mom said. "Let's put on our jackets and shoes and go outside. Maybe we can see the comet now."

Lily and Tom followed Mom outside. They looked up at the sky. They saw a bright streak of light. It was the comet. It was beautiful. It looked like a star with a long tail.

"Wow, look at that!" Lily said.

"It's amazing!" Tom said.

Mom hugged them and smiled. She said they were lucky to see the comet. She said it was a special night. She said they were safe and happy. Lily and Tom agreed. They watched the comet until it faded away. They felt warm and cozy. They thanked Mom for letting them stay up late. They went back inside and went to bed. They dreamed of the comet and the stars.

Anna and Ben were playing in the park with their dog, Max. They liked to throw a ball and watch Max run after it. Max was a good and obedient dog. He always came back when they called him.

One day, they saw a squirrel on a tree. The squirrel had a big and fluffy tail. It looked very funny and cute. Anna and Ben wanted to see it better, so they walked closer to the tree. They forgot to hold the ball.

Max saw the squirrel too. He wanted to chase it and play with it. He ran after the squirrel, leaving the ball behind. The squirrel was scared and ran away. Max followed it, barking loudly.

"Max, come back!" Anna and Ben shouted. But Max did not listen. He was too excited by the squirrel. He ran across the park, jumping over bushes and fences.

Anna and Ben ran after Max, but they could not catch him. They were worried and sad. They did not want to lose their dog.

"Where is Max?" Anna asked, looking around.

"I don't know," Ben said, wiping his tears. "Maybe he forgot us."

They heard a whistle. It was their dad. He had come to pick them up. He saw them running and looking for Max.

"What's wrong, kids?" he asked.

"We lost Max," Anna said. "He chased a squirrel and forgot us."

"Don't worry," dad said. "We'll find him. He loves you. He won't forget you."

He took their hands and walked with them. He called Max's name and looked for him.

Soon, they heard a bark. It was Max. He had found his way back to them. He was wagging his tail and licking their faces.

"Max, you're back!" Anna and Ben said, hugging him.

"I'm sorry, kids," Max said, in his doggy way. "I forgot the ball. I forgot the rules. I forgot you. But I remembered your smell. And your voice. And your love. I'm sorry. I love you."

Anna and Ben smiled. They forgave Max. They were happy to have him back.

They gave him the ball and threw it again. Max ran after it, but this time, he did not forget them. He came back when they called him. He was a good and obedient dog. He learned his lesson.

They played until it was time to go home. They thanked their dad for helping them. They said goodbye to the park and the squirrel. They went home, happy and tired. They did not forget their adventure. They did not forget each other. They were a family.

"How did you break it?" mom asked.

"We pulled it too hard," Lila and Ben said.

Lila and Ben felt bad. They said sorry to each other and hugged. They said, "We promise to be more modest, mom."

Tom and his mom were going to the airport. They had big bags and a small toy car. Tom was happy. He liked to see the big planes and the people.

"Mom, can I take my car on the plane?" Tom asked.

"Yes, you can, but you have to put it in your backpack. And you have to wipe your hands before we go in. They are dirty from playing outside," Mom said.

Tom nodded and wiped his hands on his shirt. He put his car in his backpack and zipped it up. He held Mom's hand and walked to the door.

They showed their tickets to a man. He smiled and said, "Hello, Tom. Are you ready to fly?"

Tom nodded again and said, "Yes, I am. I want to see the clouds and the birds."

The man gave them a sticker that said, "I'm flying today." He put it on Tom's shirt. Tom felt proud.

They went inside the airport. It was big and noisy. There were many people and many bags. Tom saw some shops and some food. He saw some books and some toys. He wanted to look at everything.

"Mom, can we buy something?" Tom asked.

"Maybe later, honey. We have to find our gate first. That's where we get on the plane. Come on, let's follow the signs," Mom said.

Tom followed Mom. He saw some signs with numbers and letters. He saw some pictures of planes and arrows. He saw some screens with words and colors. He tried to read them, but they were too hard.

"Mom, what do they say?" Tom asked.

"They tell us where to go and when to board. Our gate is B7. That means we have to go to the B section and find the number 7. Do you see it?" Mom said.

Tom looked around. He saw a big B and some numbers. He saw a 7. He pointed and said, "There it is, Mom. I see it."

"Good job, Tom. You are a smart boy. Let's go there and wait for our plane," Mom said.

They walked to the gate. They saw some chairs and some windows. They saw a big plane outside. It was white and blue. It had wings and a tail. It had windows and a door.

"Mom, is that our plane?" Tom asked.

"Yes, it is, Tom. That's where we are going to sit and fly. Do you like it?" Mom said.

Tom nodded and said, "I like it, Mom. It's big and pretty. Can we go now?"

"Not yet, Tom. We have to wait for our turn. They will call our names and then we can go. Do you want to sit and read a book?" Mom said.

Tom nodded and said, "Yes, please. I want to read a book about planes."

Mom took out a book from her bag. It had pictures and words about planes. She opened it and read to Tom. Tom listened and looked. He learned some new words. He learned about pilots and engines and wheels. He learned about takeoff and landing and flying.

He was happy. He liked the book. He liked the airport. He liked the plane. He was excited. He couldn't wait to fly. He hugged Mom and said, "Thank you, Mom. I love you."

Mom hugged him back and said, "I love you too, Tom. You are my brave boy. We are going to have a great trip."

One day, their cousin Lily came to visit. Lily was a mean person who did not like to share. She saw the dollhouse and wanted to play with it. She said to Sara and Ben, "This is my dollhouse now. You can't play with it. Go away!"

Sara and Ben were sad and angry. They said, "No, this is our dollhouse. We got it for our birthday. You can't spoil it. You have to share!"

But Lily did not listen. She grabbed the dollhouse and dragged it to the garden. She threw it on the ground and stomped on it. She broke the windows and the doors. She ripped the curtains and the pillows. She made the dollhouse filthy with mud and grass.

Sara and Ben ran after her and tried to stop her. They cried, "Stop, stop, you are ruining our dollhouse! You are a bad person!"

Lily laughed and said, "I don't care. I don't like your dollhouse. It is boring and ugly. I like to spoil things. It is fun!"

Sara and Ben were very sad. They hugged each other and looked at their dollhouse. It was not pretty and cozy anymore. It was dirty and broken. They wished Lily would go away and never come back. They wished they could have their dollhouse back. They wished they had a nice person to play with.

The shop lady said, "The cake with strawberries is five dollars. The cake with sprinkles is four dollars. You can add candles for one dollar more."

Lily and Sam looked at their money. They had six dollars. They wanted to buy both cakes, but they did not have enough money. They felt sad.

Mom saw them and said, "Why are you sad, my loves?"

Lily and Sam said, "We want to buy both cakes, but we do not have enough money. The price is too high."

Mom smiled and said, "Don't worry, I have a good idea. Why don't we buy one cake and share it? Then we can add candles and sing for Dad. He will love it."

Lily and Sam liked Mom's idea. They agreed to buy the cake with sprinkles, because it had more colors. They added candles and paid the shop lady. They thanked her and went home.

Lily and Sam felt happy too. They ate the cake and shared it with Mom and Dad. They had a good day.

One time, the ball went near the road. Ben ran after it, but he forgot to look both ways. He did not see the big car that was coming fast. The car hit Ben and he fell down. He was hurt and he cried.

Mia saw what happened and she was scared. She ran to Ben and tried to help him. She shouted for help. Some people came and called an ambulance. The ambulance was a big truck with a loud siren and a red cross. It came quickly and took Ben inside.

One day, they hear a loud noise from the bathroom. They wonder what it is. They run to the door and peek inside. They see a big, fierce dog in the bathtub. It is barking and splashing water everywhere.

"Whoa, look at that dog!" Ben says. "How did it get in the bathroom?"

"I don't know, maybe it came from the window," Anna says. "It looks angry and wet. We should tell Mommy."

They run to find Mommy in the kitchen. They tell her about the dog in the bathroom. Mommy is surprised and worried. She goes to the bathroom with Anna and Ben. She sees the dog and tries to calm it down.

"Hello, doggy, what are you doing here?" Mommy says. "Are you lost? Do you have a name?"

The dog stops barking and looks at Mommy. It wags its tail and licks Mommy's hand. Mommy smiles and pets the dog. She sees a tag on its collar. It says "Rex".

"Rex, you are a good dog, but you can't stay in the bathroom," Mommy says. "You need to go back to your home. I will call your owner and tell them where you are."

Mommy calls the number on the tag. She talks to Rex's owner. They say they are sorry and they will come to get Rex soon. They say Rex escaped from their yard and ran away.

Mommy hangs up the phone and tells Anna and Ben. They say goodbye to Rex and give him a hug. Rex barks and wags his tail. He is happy to see his owner again.

Mommy, Anna and Ben clean up the bathroom. They laugh and talk about their adventure. They agree that Rex was a big, fierce, but friendly dog. They hope to see him again someday.

But Ben cannot go to school now. There is a bad bug that makes people sick. Ben has to stay at home with his mom and dad. He cannot see his teacher and his friends. He cannot play with the blocks and shapes and puzzles. He cannot learn new things.

The little bird thought and decided to listen for its friends' songs. It calmed down and flew from tree to tree, listening carefully. Soon, the bird found its way back to its family and friends. The bird was happy and thanked the wise old owl.

The moral of the story is: When you are troubled, do not panic. Stay calm and think of a way to solve your problem.

The farmer was a humble man, so he agreed. The fairy said three magical words and the farmer repeated each one after her. He said them with all his might. 

Suddenly, the farmer felt a warm light surround him. He looked down and saw the corn in his field had grown tall and strong with enormous cobs. The farmer thanked the fairy, he could hardly believe it! 

The farmer repeated the three magical words every day and he soon became the most prosperous farmer in the land.

Her friend, Sarah, replied, "Trees can't sing silly. But maybe we can sing to it and make it happy."

So, they started to sing a happy song to the tree. Suddenly, the tree started to sway and rustle its leaves. It was as if the tree was singing along with them. 

From that day on, Lily and her friends would visit the tree and sing to it. They knew that even though the tree couldn't talk, it was their friend and would always listen to their songs.

Tim and Sam were two kids who liked to play with fire. They found a box of matches in the garage and decided to light them and see what would happen. They did not listen to their mom, who told them to stay away from fire and matches. They thought it was fun to watch the flames and the smoke.

One day, they went to the park with their matches. They saw a big pile of dry leaves and thought it would be a good place to burn them. They did not see that there was a sign that said "No fires allowed". They did not care about the rules or the danger. They lit a match and threw it on the leaves.

Soon, the leaves caught fire and started to burn. The fire grew bigger and bigger and spread to the grass and the trees. Tim and Sam were scared and ran away. They did not tell anyone what they had done. They did not help to put out the fire.

A polite girl named Amy saw the fire and ran to get help. She called the firemen and told them what was happening. She also told them that she saw two kids running away from the fire. She was brave and honest.

The firemen came and put out the fire. They also found Tim and Sam hiding behind a fence. They were angry and asked them why they had started the fire. Tim and Sam lied and said they did not do it. They blamed Amy and said she was the one who burned the leaves.

The firemen did not believe them. They knew that Amy was polite and told the truth. They also saw the matches in Tim and Sam's pockets. They took Tim and Sam to their mom and told her what they had done. Their mom was very sad and mad. She punished them and made them apologize to Amy and the firemen. She also made them pay for the damage they had caused.

Tim and Sam learned a hard lesson. They realized that playing with fire was not fun, but dangerous and wrong. They also realized that lying and blaming others was not smart, but cowardly and mean. They wished they had listened to their mom and been polite like Amy.

The moral of the story is: Fire can burn and hurt. Do not play with fire or matches. Listen to your mom and follow the rules. Be polite and tell the truth. Do not lie or blame others.

Lily and Max were playing in the backyard. They liked to dig in the dirt and find worms and rocks. They also liked to mix water and dirt in a big bucket and make mud pies.

"Look, I made a big mud pie!" Lily said, holding up her creation. "It has a worm and a leaf on top."

"Wow, that's a great mud pie!" Max said. "Can I have a bite?"

Lily laughed. "No, silly, you can't eat mud pies. They are only for pretend."

Max nodded. He looked around and saw a big oak tree. He had an idea. "Let's make a tree house with mud pies!" he said.

"A tree house with mud pies?" Lily asked. "How do we do that?"

Max pointed to the oak tree. "We can climb up there and stick mud pies on the branches. Then we can have a secret place to play."

Lily liked the idea. She followed Max to the oak tree. They climbed up carefully and started to stick mud pies on the branches. They had fun making walls and windows and a door.

But soon they realized that the mud pies were not very good for building. They were wet and heavy and kept falling off. They also made the branches slippery and dirty. Lily and Max felt uncomfortable and sticky.

"Maybe this was not a good idea," Lily said. "The mud pies are not staying on the tree. And we are getting all messy."

"Yeah, you're right," Max said. "The mud pies are better for the ground. And we are too high up. I'm scared."

Lily and Max decided to climb down the oak tree. They were careful not to slip or drop any mud pies. When they reached the ground, they ran to the hose and washed off the mud. They felt much better.

"Next time, let's make something else with mud pies," Lily said.

"Like what?" Max asked.

Lily thought for a moment. "Maybe a castle or a car or a dinosaur," she said.

Max smiled. "That sounds fun," he said. "Let's do that tomorrow."

Lily and Max hugged and went inside. They had a good day playing with mud pies.

Sam was not sure, but he did not want to be left out. He took a banana and peeled it. He was about to eat it when he heard a loud roar.

A big bear came out of the bushes. It saw the basket and the boys. It was angry and hungry. It wanted the meal for itself.

"I don't know," Sam said. "Maybe he is scared of the lion. Maybe he is angry at the lion. Maybe he forgot the lion."

Ben and Lily were hungry. They wanted to eat soup for dinner. But Mom was not home yet. She was working late.

"Can we make soup by ourselves?" Lily asked Ben.

Ben looked at the kitchen. He saw a big pot, some cans, and a spoon. He thought he could use them to make soup.

"Maybe we can," he said. "Let's try."

Ben and Lily opened some cans. They poured them into the pot. They added some water and salt. They turned on the stove. They waited for the soup to boil.

But they forgot to turn on the light. The kitchen was dark. They could not see the soup very well.

"Is the soup ready?" Lily asked.

"I don't know," Ben said. "Let me check."

He used the spoon to stir the soup. He lifted the spoon to his mouth. He tasted the soup.

"Yuck!" he spat. "This soup is bad!"

He looked at the spoon. He saw something green and slimy on it.

"What is this?" he cried.

Lily came closer. She saw the green thing too.

"Ew!" she screamed. "That's not soup! That's peas!"

They had used the wrong cans. They had made pea soup instead of chicken soup.

They heard the door open. Mom was home.

"Hi, kids," Mom said. "What are you doing in the dark?"

Ben and Lily ran to Mom. They hugged her.

"Mom, we tried to make soup, but we made a mistake," Ben said.

"We used peas instead of chicken," Lily said.

Mom smiled. She turned on the light. She saw the pot of pea soup.

"That's okay," she said. "Pea soup is good too. Do you want to try some?"

Ben and Lily shook their heads.

"No, thank you," they said.

Mom laughed. She hugged them.

"Then how about some pizza?" she asked.

Ben and Lily nodded.

"Yes, please!" they said.

They threw away the pea soup. They ate pizza with Mom. They were happy.

She wanted to show Ben that he was wrong. She did not look at him or at the other side of the lake. She only looked at the water.

But Ben had a plan. He did not swim as fast as he could. He swam behind Anna. He followed her. He waited for the right moment. Then he grabbed her swim cap and pulled it off. Anna felt a tug on her head. She stopped swimming. She turned around. She saw Ben holding her swim cap and laughing. He swam past her and reached the other side of the lake. He won the race.

Anna was very sad and angry. She cried. She wanted her swim cap back. She swam to the other side of the lake. She asked Ben to give her swim cap back. But Ben said no. He said he won the race and he won the swim cap. He said he would keep it. He said it was his now.

They said he did not win the race fairly. They said he should give Anna her swim cap back. But Ben said no. He said he did not care what they said. He said he was the best swimmer and he could do what he wanted.

He said he had to give Anna her swim cap back. He said he had to apologize to her and to her friends. He said he had to leave the lake and never come back. He said he was not welcome there anymore.

Ben was very scared. He did not want to leave the lake. He did not want to lose his swim cap. He did not want to apologize. But he had no choice. The lifeguard was bigger and stronger than him. He had to do what he said. He gave Anna her swim cap back. He said he was sorry. He left the lake. He never came back.

Anna was very happy. She got her swim cap back. She thanked the lifeguard. She hugged her friends. They said they were proud of her. They said she was the best swimmer and the best friend. They said they would always swim with her. They said they would always be nice to each other. They learned a lesson. They learned that cheating is wrong and that being kind is right. One day, they saw a big basket of prunes on the table. Prunes were dried plums that were wrinkly and sweet. Lila and Tom loved prunes, so they ran to the table and grabbed some.

"Yum, yum, these are so good!" Lila said.

"Let's take some more!" Tom said.

They took some more prunes and put them in their pockets. Then they went back to the garden to play.

But they did not know that the prunes were very old. They had been sitting on the table for a long time, and they had started to rot. Rot means that something is bad and smelly and has germs on it.

As they played, the prunes in their pockets got warmer and softer and more rotten. They also got sticky and messy and stained their clothes.

Soon, they started to smell something bad.

"Yuck, what is that?" Lila asked.

"I don't know, maybe it's the flowers," Tom said.

They sniffed the flowers, but they smelled nice.

"Maybe it's the dirt," Lila said.

They sniffed the dirt, but it smelled normal.

"Maybe it's us," Tom said.

They sniffed each other, and they made a face.

"Ew, it is us!" Lila said.

They looked at their pockets, and they saw the rotten prunes. They were brown and mushy and furry. Furry means that something has hair or fuzz on it. The rotten prunes had white fuzz on them, and that was mold. Mold is a kind of germ that grows on rotten things.

"Yuck, yuck, yuck!" Lila and Tom said.

They threw the rotten prunes away, and they ran to the house. They wanted to wash their clothes and their hands and their faces.

But their mom saw them, and she was not happy.

"What have you done?" she asked. "You took the prunes from the table, and you made a mess!"

She was angry, because the prunes were for the compost. Compost is a pile of old food and leaves and grass that turns into dirt for the garden. The prunes were not for eating, they were for the compost.

Lila and Tom felt sorry, and they said they were sorry.

"We didn't know, mom, we thought they were good," Lila said.

"We like prunes, mom, but not these ones," Tom said.

Mom sighed, and she said they had to learn to ask before they take something. She also said they had to help her clean the mess. She said they could have some fresh prunes later, if they were good.

Lila and Tom nodded, and they said they would. They learned their lesson, and they never took old prunes again. They only took fresh ones, and they always asked first.

One day, Tom and his mom went to the sea. They saw a big boat with many people on it. Mom said, "That is a boat for watching dolphins. Do you want to go and see them?"

Tom nodded and said, "Yes, mom. I like dolphins. They are nice and smart and fast."

Mom and Tom got on the boat and sat on the edge. The boat moved on the water. Tom looked around and saw many waves and birds. He asked, "Mom, where are the dolphins?"

Mom said, "They are in the water, Tom. Sometimes they come up to breathe and play. You have to watch carefully and you will see them."

Tom watched very carefully. He saw a splash and a fin. He pointed and said, "Mom, look! A dolphin!"

Mom looked and said, "Yes, Tom. You are right. That is a dolphin. It is gray and shiny and smooth."

Tom smiled and said, "Can I talk to the dolphin, mom?"

Mom said, "You can try, Tom. Maybe the dolphin will hear you and answer."

Tom leaned over the edge and said, "Hello, dolphin. I am Tom. I like you. Do you want to be my friend?"

The dolphin heard Tom and came closer. It made a sound like a whistle and a click. It jumped out of the water and splashed Tom and mom. Tom laughed and said, "Thank you, dolphin. You are fun. I think you are my friend."

The dolphin nodded and made another sound. It swam around the boat and showed Tom its tail and its teeth. Tom clapped and said, "Wow, dolphin. You are amazing. You can do many things."

Mom said, "Tom, you are lucky. The dolphin likes you. It is very friendly and playful. But we have to go soon. The boat will part and go back to the land."

Tom said, "Oh, mom. I don't want to go. I want to stay with the dolphin."

Mom said, "I know, Tom. But we can't stay here forever. The dolphin has to stay in the water. It has its own family and friends. Maybe we can come back another day and see it again."

Tom said, "Okay, mom. I understand. But can I say goodbye to the dolphin?"

Mom said, "Of course, Tom. You can say goodbye to the dolphin."

Tom waved and said, "Goodbye, dolphin. You are my friend. I will miss you. I hope you are happy and safe."

The dolphin waved back and said, "Goodbye, Tom. You are my friend. I will miss you too. I hope you come back and see me again."

The dolphin gave Tom a big smile and a kiss. Then it dived into the water and swam away. Tom felt sad and happy at the same time. He hugged mom and said, "Mom, that was the best day ever. I love the dolphin. And I love you."

Mom hugged Tom and said, "I love you too, Tom. And I'm glad you had fun with the dolphin. It was a very special day. Now let's go back to the land and tell dad all about it."

Tom and mom got up and went to the other side of the boat. The boat started to move and part from the sea. Tom looked back and saw the water and the sky. He thought of the dolphin and smiled. He said, "Bye, bye, sea. Bye, bye, dolphin. I will see you again."

Lila and Tom were friends who liked to play together. One day, they found a big box of toys in the park. They opened the box and saw many fun things inside. There were cars, dolls, balls, books, and more.

"Wow, look at all these toys!" Lila said. "Can we play with them?"

"Sure, why not?" Tom said. "But we have to be careful. Maybe someone left them here for a reason."

They took out some toys and started to play. Lila picked a pink sweater and put it on. She pretended to be a princess. Tom picked a fake sword and pretended to be a knight.

They had a lot of fun, but soon they got hungry and thirsty. They decided to go home and get some snacks. They left the toys in the box and walked away.

But when they came back, they saw a sad boy sitting next to the box. He was crying and holding a picture.

"Hey, what's wrong?" Lila asked.

"These are my toys," the boy said. "My mom gave them to me before she went away. She said she would come back soon, but she didn't. I miss her so much. I brought the toys here to remember her, but someone took them and played with them. They made them dirty and messy. They don't care about me or my mom."

Lila and Tom felt very sorry for the boy. They realized they had made a mistake. They had taken the toys without asking. They had not thought about how the boy would feel.

They quickly put the toys back in the box and apologized to the boy.

"We are so sorry," Lila said. "We didn't know these were your toys. We thought they were for everyone to share. We didn't mean to hurt you or your mom."

"We are very sorry," Tom said. "We should have asked you first. We should have respected your things. We were wrong to take them and play with them."

The boy looked at them and saw that they were sincere. He wiped his tears and smiled a little.

"It's okay," he said. "I forgive you. You are nice kids. Do you want to be my friends?"

Lila and Tom nodded and smiled back. They hugged the boy and said yes. They decided to play together with the toys, but this time, they asked the boy first. They also told him stories about their moms and dads. They made him feel less lonely and sad.

They learned a lesson that day. They learned to always ask before taking something that belongs to someone else. They learned to be kind and respectful to others. They learned that sharing is better than stealing. And they learned that friendship is the best gift of all.

"Ben, can you help me? This block is too heavy. I want to put it on my tower."

Ben comes over and looks at the block. He tries to lift it, but he can't either. He has an idea.

"Maybe we can roll it. Let's push it together."

They push the block with their hands, but it doesn't move. They push harder, but it still doesn't move. Ben has another idea.

"Maybe we can use our thumbs. Let's push it with our thumbs."

They put their thumbs on the block and push. The block starts to roll. They push it all the way to Sara's tower. They are happy.

"Yay, we did it! Now we can put it on the tower."

They lift the block together and put it on the tower. The tower is very tall and has a gray block on top. They are proud of their tower.

"Look at our tower! It is the best tower ever!"

They hug each other and smile. They like to play with blocks. They like to help each other. They are good friends.

Tom and Lily were having a picnic in the park. They had sandwiches, apples, and cookies. They also had a bag of peanuts to share.

"Can I have some peanuts, please?" Lily asked Tom.

"Sure, here you go," Tom said, giving her a handful of peanuts.

Lily put a peanut in her mouth and chewed. She made a funny face and spit it out.

"Yuck! This peanut is spicy!" she said.

Tom looked at the bag of peanuts. He saw a red label that said "hot and spicy".

"Oops, I think we took the wrong bag. These are not our peanuts. These are daddy's peanuts. He likes spicy food," Tom said.

"Who gave us these peanuts?" Lily asked.

"I don't know. Maybe someone at the store made a mistake. Or maybe someone played a trick on us," Tom said.

Just then, they heard a loud noise. It was a big dog barking. The dog ran towards them and jumped on their picnic blanket. He knocked over their sandwiches, apples, and cookies. He also grabbed the bag of peanuts and ran away.

"Hey, stop! That's our picnic!" Tom shouted.

The dog did not listen. He ran away with the bag of peanuts in his mouth.

"Wow, that dog disturbed our picnic. He took our spicy peanuts," Lily said.

"Maybe he likes spicy food, too. Or maybe he will learn his lesson," Tom said.

Tom and Lily looked at their messy picnic. They felt sad and angry.

"Let's go home and tell mommy and daddy what happened. Maybe they will give us some ice cream to make us feel better," Lily said.

"OK, let's go. And next time, let's check the label before we take the peanuts," Tom said.

They packed their things and walked home. They hoped the dog would not disturb them again.

"Worm is bad for the bird!" Lily says. "It is slimy and dirty!"

"Broccoli is better!"

"No, worm is better!"

"Broccoli!"

"Worm!"

Lily was a bird who loved to sing. She had a beautiful voice and a big dream. She wanted to sing in front of many other birds and make them happy. But she had a problem. She was very shy and scared of what they would think of her. She thought they would laugh at her or say mean things.

One day, she saw a poster for a singing contest. The winner would get a shiny medal and a chance to sing at the big tree, where all the birds gathered. Lily wanted to join, but she was too nervous. She hid behind a bush and watched as other birds signed up. She saw a big crow, a loud parrot, and a colorful peacock. They all looked confident and proud. Lily felt small and plain.

She was about to give up and fly away, when she heard a voice. It was her friend, Ben, a friendly sparrow. He saw her hiding and flew over to her. "Hi, Lily," he said. "Are you going to join the contest? You have a wonderful voice. You should share it with everyone."

Lily shook her head. "No, Ben, I can't. I'm too scared. What if I make a mistake? What if they don't like me? What if I embarrass myself?"

Ben smiled and gave her a gentle nudge. "Lily, you don't have to be scared. You have a gift. You have to believe in yourself. And you have me. I'll be there to support you. Come on, let's sign up together. It'll be fun."

Lily looked at Ben. He was her best friend. He always cheered her up and made her laugh. He was brave and kind. Maybe he was right. Maybe she could do it. She took a deep breath and nodded. "Okay, Ben. Let's do it."

They flew to the poster and wrote their names. Lily felt a flutter in her chest. She was excited and nervous. She hoped she wouldn't regret it.

The next day, the contest began. Many birds came to watch and cheer. Lily and Ben waited for their turn. They saw the other singers perform. Some were good, some were bad, some were funny, some were boring. Lily felt more and more nervous. She wished she could fly away.

Finally, it was their turn. They flew to the stage and faced the crowd. Lily felt her wing tremble. She looked at Ben. He smiled and winked. He whispered, "You can do it, Lily. Just sing from your heart."

Lily closed her eyes and opened her mouth. She sang the first note. It was clear and sweet. She sang the second note. It was high and strong. She sang the third note. It was low and soft. She sang the whole song. It was beautiful and touching. She sang with her heart. She forgot about her fear. She felt happy and free.

She opened her eyes and saw the crowd. They were clapping and cheering. They were smiling and crying. They loved her. They loved her voice. They loved her song. Lily felt a warm glow in her chest. She looked at Ben. He was clapping and cheering too. He was proud and happy for her. He flew to her and hugged her. He said, "You did it, Lily. You were amazing. You were successful."

Lily hugged him back. She said, "Thank you, Ben. You were right. I had to believe in myself. And I had you. You were my friend. You were my wing."

They flew to the ground and received their medal. They shared it and wore it around their necks. They felt happy and proud. They learned a lesson. They learned that fear can be overcome with courage, that talent can be shared with joy, and that friendship can be a wing.

"Lily's worm wins! Lily's worm wins!" Lily cheers.

"OK, Ben. But I don't think water will help your worm. My worm is still better. It does not need water. It is already wet and slippery," Lily says.

Flutter said, "Don't worry, Buzz. I know how to avoid spiders. Let's fly away from here." They flew away quickly, feeling safe and happy.

Tim and Sam are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a worm on the ground. Tim wants to catch the worm. He thinks it is fun. Sam does not want to catch the worm. He thinks it is mean.

Tim runs to the worm and grabs it. He laughs and shows it to Sam. Sam shakes his head and says, "No, Tim. Put the worm back. The worm is deaf. It cannot hear you. It cannot talk to you. It is scared of you. You hurt the worm."

Tim does not listen to Sam. He thinks Sam is silly. He says, "I don't care. The worm is just a worm. It is not a friend. It is not a pet. It is a toy. I can do what I want with it."

Tim puts the worm in his pocket and runs away. Sam is sad. He follows Tim. He wants to help the worm. He sees Tim go to the pond. He sees Tim take the worm out of his pocket. He sees Tim throw the worm into the water. He hears Tim say, "Bye-bye, worm. Have fun in the pond."

Sam is angry. He says, "Tim, you are bad. You are not a good friend. You are not a good person. You do not care about the worm. You do not care about anyone. The worm is not a toy. The worm is alive. The worm needs the ground. The worm cannot swim. The worm will die in the pond."

Tim is surprised. He looks at the pond. He sees the worm sink. He sees the worm stop moving. He feels sorry. He says, "Oh, no. I did not know. I did not mean to. I was just playing. I am sorry, Sam. I am sorry, worm."

Sam says, "It is too late, Tim. You cannot say sorry now. You cannot bring the worm back. You have to be careful. You have to be kind. You have to respect all living things. They are not toys. They are not yours. They have feelings. They have rights. They deserve love."

Tim nods. He says, "You are right, Sam. I was wrong. I was selfish. I was cruel. I will not do it again. I will learn from my mistake. I will be a better friend. I will be a better person. I will be more like you."

Sam smiles. He says, "Thank you, Tim. I forgive you. I am still your friend. I hope you will be mine. I hope you will be the worm's friend too. I hope you will remember the worm. I hope you will remember this day. I hope you will remember this lesson."

The end.

"Look, Lily, this is a mirror. It shows us how we look. Do you want to see?" Sara said to Lily. She held Lily in front of the mirror and smiled.

But Sara did not see her smile in the mirror. She saw a pale face with dark eyes and a frown. She saw a black dress and a black hat. She saw a doll that was not Lily.

Sara was scared. She dropped Lily and ran away from the mirror. She screamed for her mom.

"Mom, mom, there is a bad lady in the mirror! She took Lily! Help me, mom!"

Mom heard Sara and came to her room. She saw Sara crying and Lily on the floor. She saw the mirror and the pale lady.

Mom was angry. She knew who the pale lady was. She was her sister, who liked to play tricks on her and Sara. She had put the mirror in Sara's room to scare her.

Mom grabbed the mirror and turned it around. She saw her sister's face on the other side. She scolded her sister and told her to leave.

"Go away, you mean lady! You are not welcome here! You scared my Sara and hurt her Lily! How dare you!"

Mom's sister was sorry. She said she was just joking and she did not mean to make Sara cry. She said she would never do it again. She gave Lily back to Sara and apologized.

Sara was still scared, but she was happy to have Lily back. She hugged Lily and thanked mom. Mom hugged Sara and told her she loved her. She threw the mirror away and took Sara and Lily to the kitchen for a snack. Sara never saw the pale lady again.

They learned their lesson. They also learned that honey is sticky and hard to clean.

Lily looked at Tom's tower. She liked it, but she wanted to make her own tower. She saw some green and purple and orange blocks that Tom did not use. She reached for them.

"Hey, those are my blocks!" Tom said. "You cannot take them. They are part of my tower."

"But you did not use them!" Lily said. "They are separate from your tower. I want to use them for my tower."

Tom and Lily started to argue. They pulled and pushed the blocks. They did not want to share. They were restless and angry.

Suddenly, they heard a loud crash. They turned around and saw that their towers had fallen down. The blocks were scattered all over the floor. They had broken their towers.

Tom and Lily felt sad and sorry. They looked at each other.

"I am sorry, Tom," Lily said. "I should have asked you before I took your blocks. Can we share them and build a new tower together?"

"I am sorry, Lily," Tom said. "I should have let you use some of my blocks. They are more fun when we share them. Can we be friends and build a new tower together?"

Tom and Lily smiled and nodded. They hugged and said sorry. They picked up the blocks and started to build a new tower together. They used all the colors and shapes. They made the tower bigger and better than before. They were happy and proud. They had learned to share.

Tom and Lily were playing by the pond. They liked to throw stones and watch the water splash. They did not see the big alligator hiding under the water. The alligator was hungry and wanted to eat them.

"Look, Lily, I found a big stone!" Tom said. He threw the stone as hard as he could. It landed near the alligator's nose. The alligator was angry and opened his mouth wide. He showed his sharp teeth and hissed.

"Tom, Lily, run!" their mom shouted. She saw the alligator and was scared. She ran to them and grabbed their hands. They ran away from the pond as fast as they could.

The alligator was too slow to catch them. He closed his mouth and swam away. He looked for other food.

Tom and Lily were safe with their mom. They hugged her and said sorry.

"Sorry, mom, we did not know there was an alligator," Tom said.

"Sorry, mom, we did not listen to you when you told us to stay away from the pond," Lily said.

"It's okay, my loves, I'm glad you are okay," their mom said. "But you have to be careful and obey me. The pond is not a safe place to play. The alligator is mighty and can hurt you."

Tom and Lily nodded. They learned their lesson. They never played by the pond again. They played in the yard instead, where there were no alligators.

Timmy asked Lily if he could see her necklace and she happily showed it to him. But then, Timmy grabbed the necklace and ran away with it. Lily was very sad and cried a lot.

Lily's mom comforted her and told her that sometimes we learn that not everyone is nice and we have to be careful with our special things. Lily learned a valuable lesson that day, but she still missed her lovely necklace.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny named Bun. Bun was very tired and needed a nap. He looked for a cozy spot to nap in, but all the spots were taken. Finally, he found a spot in the east side of the meadow. It was a little dirty and filthy, but Bun didn't care because he was so tired.

As he was napping, he woke up to find a group of animals playing nearby. They were having so much fun and Bun wanted to join in. But when he tried to play with them, they made fun of him for napping in such a dirty spot. Bun felt sad and ashamed.

He realized that it's better to take a nap in a clean spot than a dirty one. He also learned that it's important to not judge others for where they choose to nap. From that day on, Bun made sure to take his naps in a clean and cozy spot, and he never made fun of anyone for where they chose to rest.

He said, "No, we have to be nice to the bird. Let's just move away from the pole and let it fly by." So they all moved away from the pole and the bird flew by safely. Timmy felt happy that they didn't hurt the bird.

The bad ending is that Timmy had to go to the hospital and get a cast on his arm. He couldn't play with his wagon for a long time.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside, but he never wanted to take a bath. His mom would always tell him, "Timmy, you need to take a bath. You're too dirty!"

One day, Timmy went to play with his friend Billy. Billy asked Timmy, "Why do you never take a bath?" Timmy replied, "I don't like it. It's boring."

Billy said, "That's not the truth. You don't take a bath because you're afraid to sleep alone at night. But you know what? If you take a bath, you'll feel clean and cozy in your bed. You won't be afraid anymore."

Timmy thought about it and realized that Billy was right. He took a bath that night and felt so clean and cozy in his bed. He wasn't afraid to sleep alone anymore. From that day on, Timmy took a bath every night and felt much better. The truth was, taking a bath wasn't so bad after all.

"I'm playing! Do you want to play with me?" replied Tweetie.

"Sure! But first, let's cook something yummy to eat," said Whiskers.

So they went to the kitchen and cooked some tasty fish. While they were eating, Tweetie noticed a feather on the floor.

"Look, Whiskers! A feather! Can we play with it?" asked Tweetie excitedly.

"Of course! Let's play catch with it," said Whiskers.

And so, they played and had fun until it was time for Tweetie to go back to her nest. She thanked Whiskers for the fun day and promised to come back and play again soon.

Once upon a time there was a puppy called Spot. Spot was naughty. He had a bad habit of poking things. One day he saw a big bone on the ground and he poked it with his paw. Suddenly, a loud voice came from the bone. "Stop poking me!" it said. Spot was so scared that he fell over. He looked to see who was talking. A small ghost was floating in the air.

"Why did you poke me?" the ghost asked. Spot felt very guilty, so he said nothing.

The ghost continued, "I know you didn't mean to. I am sorry I scared you. You can keep the bone as a reminder not to do it again."

Spot thanked the ghost and took the bone home. He never poked anything ever again. The end.

"Maybe for your birthday, Sam. That car is very expensive," Mom said.

Sam felt sad. He wished he had the car now. He went home and played with his other cars, but he could not stop thinking about the white car.

That night, Sam had a dream. He dreamed that he had the white car, and he was driving it on an icy road. The road was slippery and sparkly, and the car was fast and smooth. Sam felt happy and excited. He saw other cars on the road, but they were not as cool as his car. He passed them all with a loud honk.

"Beep beep! Out of my way!" he shouted.

He came to a big hill, and he pressed the gas pedal. The car went up the hill, and then flew in the air. Sam felt like he was flying too. He looked out the window, and saw a beautiful winter wonderland. He saw snowmen, and penguins, and a big castle made of ice.

"Wow! This is amazing!" he said.

He landed on the other side of the hill, and drove towards the castle. He wanted to see what was inside. He imagined that there were more toys and surprises waiting for him. He smiled and drove faster.

He was almost there, when he heard a loud noise. It was his alarm clock, ringing in his room. Sam woke up, and rubbed his eyes. He realized that it was all a dream. He felt sad again. He wished he could go back to the icy road and the castle.

He looked at his model cars, lying on the floor. He saw his favorite red car, and his blue car, and his green car. He picked them up, and put them on his bed. He decided to play with them again. He thought that maybe he could imagine that they were white cars, and that he was driving them on an icy road. He thought that maybe he could have fun with them, even if they were not the car he wanted.

He smiled, and said to himself, "Maybe for my birthday."

Lily was a girl who liked to write in her diary every day. She wrote about her friends, her toys, her dreams and her feelings. She kept her diary in a secret place under her bed, and she never let anyone see it.

One day, her brother Tom was bored and curious. He wanted to know what Lily wrote in her diary. He sneaked into her room and looked under her bed. He found the diary and opened it. He read some of the pages and laughed. He thought Lily was silly and childish. He decided to tease her about it.

He waited for Lily to come home from school. When she arrived, he ran to her and said, "Lily, I know your secret. I read your diary. You are so funny. You write about stupid things. You have a crush on Sam. You are afraid of the dark. You wish you had a pony. Ha ha ha!"

Lily was shocked and angry. She felt hurt and betrayed. She asked Tom, "Why did you read my diary? That is not nice. That is not fair. That is my private thing. You should not do that. You should say sorry."

But Tom did not say sorry. He did not care. He kept laughing and making fun of her. He said, "I don't care. Your diary is boring and dumb. You are a baby. You should grow up. You should not write in a diary. You should play with me and my friends. We have fun. We play games. We are cool."

Lily ran to her room and cried. She felt sad and lonely. She did not want to play with Tom or his friends. She did not want to write in her diary anymore. She felt like she had no one to trust or talk to. She felt like she had lost something important.

The moral of the story is: You should not read other people's diaries. It is rude and mean. It can hurt their feelings and break their trust. You should respect their privacy and their choices. You should be kind and honest. You should say sorry if you make a mistake. You should try to understand and appreciate them. You should be a good brother or sister.
