Lila and Tom are twins. They like to play in the park with their mom. One day, they see a big gray bird on a tree. The bird has a long tail and a red head. It makes a loud noise.

"Look, mom, a parrot!" Lila says.

"Can we talk to it?" Tom asks.

Mom nods. "You can try, but you have to listen carefully. Parrots can copy what you say, but they don't always understand."

Lila and Tom go closer to the tree. They say hello to the parrot. The parrot says hello back. They laugh. They ask the parrot its name. The parrot says its name is Pepper.

"Pepper, do you like to eat?" Lila asks.

"Yes, I like to eat. I like spicy food. Do you have spicy food?" the parrot says.

Lila and Tom shake their heads. They don't like spicy food. Spicy food makes their mouths hurt. They like sweet food, like apples and cookies.

"We have apples and cookies. Do you want some?" Tom offers.

The parrot shakes its head. "No, thank you. I don't like sweet food. Sweet food makes me sick. I like spicy food, like chili and curry."

Lila and Tom look at each other. They don't know what chili and curry are. They sound spicy. They wonder if the parrot can eat them.

"Mom, can parrots eat chili and curry?" they ask.

Mom smiles. "Yes, they can. Parrots have different tastes than us. They like spicy food because it helps them stay healthy and warm. But we have to be careful not to give them too much, or they might get thirsty."

Lila and Tom nod. They learn something new. They like the parrot. They say goodbye to the parrot. The parrot says goodbye back. They wave and walk away.

"Maybe we can bring some spicy food for Pepper next time," Lila says.

"Maybe," Tom says. "But I still like apples and cookies better."

"Come in, come in. What's wrong?" Mr. Jones asked.

"There's a crocodile in the pond. It's big and mean. It tried to eat us," Lily and Ben said.

"A crocodile? In the pond? That's impossible. There are no crocodiles in this park," Mr. Jones said.

"Wow, you're right. There is a crocodile in the pond. How did it get there?" Mr. Jones said.

He called the zoo and the police. They came and caught the crocodile. They took it away to a safe place. They thanked Lily and Ben for telling them.

Lily and Ben were happy. They were safe and brave. They hugged Mr. Jones and his dog. They thanked him for helping them.

The goat looked at the flowers and snorted. He did not want the flowers. He wanted the grass. He pushed the fence with his horns and made a hole. He ran through the hole and into the field. He ate all the flowers that Tom and Sue had picked.

"Hey, stop that!" Tom shouted. "Those are our flowers. You are a bad goat!"

The goat did not stop. He ate and ate until there were no more flowers left. He was very full and happy. He went back to the fence and looked at Tom and Sue. They were very sad and angry. They had no more flowers to play with.

"Sorry, kids," the goat said. "I was hungry and I like flowers. They are tasty and pretty. But I was not nice to you. I should have shared the grass with you. Can you forgive me?"

Tom and Sue looked at each other. They were still upset, but they also felt sorry for the goat. He seemed troubled and sorry.

"Okay, goat," Sue said. "We forgive you. But next time, please ask before you take something that is not yours. And maybe you can try something new, like carrots or apples. They are good for you and for us."

"Thank you, kids," the goat said. "You are very kind and smart. I will try to be more polite and curious. And maybe we can be friends."

The moral of the story is: Don't be greedy and selfish. Share what you have and try new things. You might make new friends and have more fun.

Lily thought about it and said, "Wow, that truck must be really strong and flexible to carry such heavy things!" Her friend agreed and they continued playing together, happy to enjoy the simple joys of childhood.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to sing songs all day long. One day, Lily's mommy had to go to work, and Lily felt sad. "Mommy, don't go," she said. "I don't want to be alone."

"Don't worry, Lily," mommy said. "You can be independent and play with your toys. I'll be back soon."

Lily tried to play, but she felt lonely. Suddenly, she heard a knock on the door. It was her neighbor, Mrs. Smith. "Hi, Lily," she said. "I heard you singing earlier. Would you like to sing a song with me?"

Lily felt happy and comforted. She sang a song with Mrs. Smith, and they had lots of fun. From that day on, Lily didn't feel scared to be independent, because she knew that her neighbors were always there to comfort her.

Once upon a time, there was an elderly lady named Granny who lived in a big house with a porch. She loved to sit on her porch and watch the world go by. One day, a little boy named Timmy came to visit her.

"Hello, Granny," said Timmy. "Can we play together?"

"Of course, we can," replied Granny. "Let's play a game of balance. I have a special toy for you."

Granny gave Timmy a toy that had a ball on one side and a stick on the other. Timmy tried to balance the ball on the stick, but he found it difficult.

"Don't worry," said Granny. "You will get better with practice."

Suddenly, a gust of wind blew and the ball fell off the stick. Timmy was upset, but Granny consoled him and said, "It's okay, Timmy. Sometimes things don't go as planned, but we can always try again."

From that day on, Timmy visited Granny often and they played many games together. Timmy became better at balancing the ball on the stick, and Granny was happy to have a new friend to share her porch with.

From that day on, Lily knew that even if something seemed difficult, she could do it if she tried. Her mommy was happy too, and gave her a big hug. The moral of the story is that we can accomplish anything if we try our best.

On the hill, Tim met a girl named Sue. She was making a big snowman. Tim was envious of Sue's snowman. He wanted to make one too. So, he asked Sue, "Can I help you make the snowman?"

Sue said, "Yes, Tim! Let's make the biggest snowman ever!" They worked together to make the snowman. They used sticks for arms and a carrot for the nose. The snowman was so big, it could almost touch the sky!

As they were playing, the wind started to blow. It was getting colder, and the snow began to freeze. Tim and Sue knew it was time to go home. They said goodbye to each other and promised to play again soon.

When Tim got home, he told his mom all about his day at the park. He was happy he made a new friend and built the biggest snowman ever.

One day, a bird and a bee were talking. The bird said, "I wish I could touch the sky." The bee said, "I can help you, but it might hurt."

The bird thought for a moment and said, "I don't care, I want to touch the sky." So the bee helped the bird to fly higher and higher. The bird was happy, but it started to feel hurt.

The bird regretted flying so high. It was cold and hurt a lot. The bird fell down and could not fly anymore. The bee was sad and said, "I told you it might hurt."

The moral of the story is to listen to your friends when they warn you about something, because they might be right.

Once upon a time, there was an orange named Mr. Orange. Mr. Orange lived in a big tree with his friends. They all played together and had fun every day. But one day, Mr. Orange felt troubled. He didn't know why.

Mr. Orange went to his friend, the apple. "I feel troubled," said Mr. Orange. "Can you help me?" The apple thought for a moment, then said, "Let's turn around and around. Maybe that will help you feel better." So they turned around and around, but Mr. Orange still felt troubled.

Next, Mr. Orange went to his friend, the banana. "I feel troubled," said Mr. Orange. "Can you help me?" The banana thought for a moment, then said, "Let's turn upside down. Maybe that will help you feel better." So they turned upside down, but Mr. Orange still felt troubled. Then, Mr. Orange went to his friend, the grape. "I feel troubled," said Mr. Orange. From that day on, Mr. Orange and his friends knew that turning and jumping could help them feel better when they were troubled.

One day, a hungry raven saw a big apple on a tree. He wanted to eat it, but it was too high for him. He looked around and saw a fox on the ground. He had an idea.

"Hello, fox," he said. "Do you want to share this apple with me? It is very sweet and juicy."

The fox looked up and saw the apple. He licked his lips. He wanted to eat it, too, but he could not climb the tree.

"Sure, raven," he said. "How can we get it?"

"Easy," the raven said. "You just have to help me. I will fly up and peck the apple until it falls. Then you can catch it and split it with me. Half for you, half for me. Deal?"

"Deal," the fox said. He smiled, but he was not honest. He wanted to eat the whole apple by himself.

The raven flew up and pecked the apple. It was hard and firm, but he did not give up. He pecked and pecked until the apple fell. The fox was ready. He jumped and caught the apple in his mouth.

"Hey, fox, give me my half!" the raven cried.

"Sorry, raven, no can do," the fox said. "This apple is mine. You can have the seeds, if you want. They are good for you."

The fox ran away with the apple, leaving the raven with nothing. The raven was angry and sad. He had been tricked by the fox. He learned a lesson: do not trust a greedy fox. He flew away, still hungry and alone. The end.

Ben did not know. He had heard the word before, but he did not know what it meant. He thought it was a kind of plant that lived in the desert. He wanted to touch it and see how it felt.

"Let's go closer," he said.

Mia was not sure. She thought the plant looked scary. She did not want to touch it. She was afraid it would hurt her.

"Maybe we should not," she said.

Ben did not listen. He ran to the plant and reached out his hand. He wanted to be brave and curious. He thought Mia would be impressed.

"Look, Mia, look!" he said.

But Mia did not look. She heard Ben scream. She turned around and saw him crying. He had touched the cactus and the sharp points had poked his hand. There was blood on his hand and on the cactus.

"Ben, Ben, are you okay?" Mia said. She ran to him and hugged him. She was scared and sorry.

Ben was not okay. He was in pain and he was angry. He blamed Mia for his mistake. He thought she had dared him to touch the cactus. He thought she had been mean to him.

"Go away, Mia, go away!" he said. He pushed her away. He did not want her hug. He did not want her help. He did not want her friendship.

Mia was hurt and sad. She did not understand why Ben was mad at her. She had been kind to him. She had tried to warn him. She had tried to comfort him. She had been his friend.

But Ben did not care. He ran away from Mia and from the cactus. He ran to his mom and told her what happened. He did not tell her the truth. He lied and said Mia had pushed him to the cactus. He said Mia had been bad to him.

Mia was left alone in the park. She looked at the cactus and at her empty hand. She wished Ben had not touched the cactus. She wished Ben had not lied. She wished Ben had been her friend.

But Ben was not her friend. He was her enemy. He had hurt himself and he had hurt her. He had broken their friendship.

"I don't know, but I don't like it. The jelly is moving!" Mia says.

"Help! Help! The jelly is too powerful!" Tim and Mia scream.

"Yes, Mom, I'm ready!" Anna said. She hugged her teddy bear and put on her coat. She was a little nervous about riding the bus, but Mom said it would be fun.

They walked to the bus stop and waited for the bus. Anna saw a lot of cars and people on the street. She heard a lot of noises and smells. She held Mom's hand tightly.

"Look, Anna, there's the bus!" Mom said. She waved to the bus driver and helped Anna get on the bus. They found two seats and sat down. Anna looked out the window and saw the buildings and trees go by.

"Mom, how long will it take to get to grandma's house?" Anna asked.

"Not too long, sweetie. Maybe an hour or so. Do you want to read a book or play with your toys?" Mom asked.

"I want to read a book, Mom. Can you read it to me?" Anna asked.

"Of course, Anna. Which one do you want?" Mom asked.

Anna picked a book about a dog who was very helpful. He helped his friends and his family with different things. He helped a cat who was stuck in a tree, a bird who lost her nest, and a mouse who was hungry. He was very kind and brave.

Anna liked the story very much. She liked the dog and his friends. She wanted to be helpful too.

"Mom, can I be helpful like the dog?" Anna asked.

"Sure, Anna. You are already very helpful. You help me with chores, you share your toys, and you make nice cards. You are a very good girl." Mom said.

"Thank you, Mom. I love you." Anna said.

"I love you too, Anna. And you know who else loves you?" Mom asked.

"Who, Mom?" Anna asked.

"Grandma, of course. She can't wait to see you. She has a surprise for you." Mom said.

"A surprise? What is it, Mom?" Anna asked.

"I don't know, Anna. You have to wait and see. But I promise you, you will like it." Mom said.

"Okay, Mom. I can't wait to see grandma and her surprise. I'm so excited!" Anna said.

They smiled at each other and hugged. They were almost there. They were going to have a wonderful visit.

Anna and Ben are playing in the park. They see a big pole that holds a swing. Anna wants to climb the pole. She thinks it is fun and cool.

"Look, Ben, I can climb the pole!" Anna says. She puts her hands and feet on the pole and tries to go up.

Ben does not want to climb the pole. He thinks it is hard and uncomfortable. He likes to swing and slide.

"Anna, come down, the pole is not good. It is cold and rough. It hurts your skin. Come and swing with me!" Ben says.

Anna does not listen to Ben. She wants to reach the top of the pole. She climbs higher and higher. But then she feels something wet and sticky on the pole. It is bird poop. It is gross and smelly.

"Yuck, yuck, yuck!" Anna screams. She lets go of the pole and falls down. She lands on the grass. She is dirty and unhappy.

"Are you okay, Anna?" Ben asks. He runs to her and helps her get up.

"I am okay, but I am sorry, Ben. You were right. The pole is not good. It is bad and nasty. I do not want to climb it anymore. I want to swing with you!" Anna says.

Ben smiles and hugs Anna. He is glad that she is okay and that she changed her mind.

"Come on, Anna, let's swing. It is fun and nice. It makes you fly and laugh. It is better than the pole!" Ben says.

Anna and Ben go to the swing. They swing high and low. They have fun and forget about the pole. They are happy and friends.

"Wow, look at all the yummy food!" Sara said. "Let's take some and eat them!"

"No, Sara, we can't do that!" Ben said. "This basket belongs to someone else. Maybe they are having a picnic. It is not nice to take things that are not ours."

But Sara did not listen to Ben. She lifted the basket and ran away with it. Ben followed her, feeling sad and scared.

Soon, they heard a loud voice behind them. It was a man with a big hat and a red shirt. He was the owner of the basket. He was angry and shouted at them.

"Hey, you little thieves! Give me back my basket! That is my lunch! How dare you steal from me!"

Sara and Ben were very sorry and afraid. They dropped the basket and said sorry to the man. The man took his basket and told them to never do that again. He said stealing is bad and wrong. He said they should always be honest and respectful.

Tim and Lily were playing in the park. They saw a big sack under a tree. They wanted to see what was inside.

"Let's open it!" Tim said.

"Maybe it has toys or candy!" Lily said.

They ran to the sack and pulled the string. But when they opened it, they saw a long, scaly snake. It hissed and showed its teeth.

"Ah! A snake!" Tim and Lily screamed.

They dropped the sack and ran away. The snake slithered out of the sack and followed them.

"Help! Help!" Tim and Lily shouted.

A man heard them and came to see what was wrong. He saw the snake and grabbed a stick. He hit the snake and made it go away.

"Are you okay, kids?" the man asked.

"Yes, thank you!" Tim and Lily said.

"Where did you find that snake?" the man asked.

"In that sack, under the tree. It was mysterious!" Tim said.

"That's not a sack, that's a pillowcase. And that's not a snake, that's a python. Someone must have left it here by mistake. It's very dangerous!" the man said.

"Wow, a python! That's a big snake!" Lily said.

"Yes, it is. You should never touch a snake, especially a python. They can bite and squeeze you. You were very lucky!" the man said.

He took the pillowcase and the python and called the animal control. Tim and Lily learned a lesson. They never opened a mysterious sack again.

Lily was a little girl who liked to draw. She had many crayons and papers in her room. She drew flowers, animals, houses and people. She wanted to be a painter when she grew up.

One day, she went to the park with her mom. She saw a man with a big easel and a brush. He was painting a picture of the trees and the sky. Lily was curious. She walked over to the man and said, "Hello, what are you doing?"

The man smiled and said, "Hello, little one. I am a painter. I am making a picture with paint and a brush. Do you like to draw?"

Lily nodded and said, "Yes, I do. I have many crayons and papers. I draw flowers, animals, houses and people. I want to be a painter like you."

The man said, "That's wonderful. You have a lot of imagination and talent. Would you like to try my brush and paint?"

Lily said, "Yes, please. Can I?"

The man said, "Of course. Here, you can use this canvas. It is a white paper that you can paint on. You can choose any color you want from my palette. It is a board with many paints on it. Be careful, though. The paint is wet and sticky. It can make a mess."

Lily said, "Thank you. I will be careful. I will paint a picture of you and me in the park."

The man said, "That sounds lovely. I can't wait to see it."

Lily took the brush and the palette and started to paint. She dipped the brush in the paint and made strokes on the canvas. She painted the man's face, his hat, his shirt and his easel. She painted herself, her dress, her hair and her smile. She painted the trees, the sky, the grass and the flowers. She used many colors and made a bright and happy picture.

When she was done, she showed the man her picture. The man said, "Wow, that's amazing. You are a very good painter, Lily. You have made a beautiful picture of us in the park. I love it. Can I keep it?"

Lily said, "Yes, you can. It is a gift for you. You are my new friend. I am happy to meet you."

The man said, "Thank you, Lily. You are my new friend, too. I am happy to meet you. You have made my day. Can I give you something in return?"

Lily said, "Yes, you can. Can you teach me more about painting? Can you show me how to mix colors and make shapes and shadows?"

The man said, "Sure, I can. I would love to teach you more about painting. You are a fast learner and a keen student. Come, let's sit down and talk more. I have some books and magazines that you can look at. They have many pictures of different painters and their works. You can learn a lot from them."

Lily said, "Thank you. That sounds fun. I want to learn more. I want to be a great painter like you."

The man said, "You're welcome. That's a good goal. I'm sure you will be a great painter one day. You have a lot of potential and passion. Just keep practicing and enjoying what you do. And remember, painting is not only a skill, but also a way of expressing yourself and your feelings. Painting is a way of making the world more beautiful and colorful."

Lily said, "I understand. Painting is a way of making the world more beautiful and colorful. I like that. I like painting. And I like you. You are a nice painter and a nice friend."

The man said, "I like you, too. You are a nice girl and a nice friend. And a nice painter. You have made me proud and happy. Thank you, Lily."

They hugged and smiled. They looked at their picture and admired it. They had met each other by chance, but they had found a common bond. They had found a new friend and a new joy. They had found painting.

Lila and Ben were twins who liked to explore the forest near their home. One day, they found a big mushroom that was red and white and had spots. It looked very unique and pretty.

"Wow, look at this mushroom!" Lila said. "It is so different from the others. I want to take it home and display it in my room."

"No, you can't do that," Ben said. "The mushroom belongs to the forest. It is part of nature. If you take it away, it might die or make you sick. And maybe other animals or plants need it too."

Lila did not listen to Ben. She picked up the mushroom and put it in her backpack. She ran back to the house, leaving Ben behind. She was very happy and proud of her mushroom.

She put the mushroom on a shelf in her room and admired it. She thought it was the most beautiful thing she ever saw. She did not notice that the mushroom started to wilt and turn brown. She did not notice that it smelled bad and had bugs on it. She did not notice that she felt itchy and sneezy.

The next day, Ben came to visit Lila. He saw the mushroom on the shelf and was shocked. He saw that Lila was sick and unhappy. He felt sorry for her and for the mushroom.

"Lila, I told you not to take the mushroom," Ben said. "It was not a good idea. The mushroom was unique and special, but it was not meant for you. It was meant for the forest. You should have left it there, where it could grow and live and help other things. That would have been better for everyone."

Lila realized that Ben was right. She felt bad for what she did. She apologized to Ben and to the mushroom. She asked Ben to help her take the mushroom back to the forest. She hoped that it was not too late.

They went to the forest and found the spot where they saw the mushroom. They gently placed the mushroom on the ground and covered it with some leaves. They said sorry to the mushroom and thanked it for its beauty. They hoped that it would recover and be happy again.

Lila and Ben learned a lesson that day. They learned to respect and appreciate nature and not to take what is not theirs. They learned that being unique is not always better than being part of something bigger. They learned that displaying something is not as good as sharing it.

He went to Lily and licked her face. He took her half of the stick and ran to Ben. He dropped the stick and licked his face too. He wanted them to chase him and have fun.

Tom and Amy were twins who liked to play in the kitchen. They liked to open the drawers and the cupboards and see what was inside. One day, they saw a big white box in the corner. It had a handle and a lock.

"What is that?" Tom asked.

"I don't know. Let's see," Amy said. She pulled the handle, but it did not move. She tried again, but it was still stuck.

"Maybe it's a freezer," Tom said. "Mommy puts food in the freezer to keep it cold."

"Maybe there's ice cream in there," Amy said. "I want ice cream."

"Me too," Tom said. "Let's find the key."

They looked around the kitchen, but they could not find the key. They saw a shiny thing on the counter. It was a spoon.

"Maybe this can open the lock," Tom said. He took the spoon and tried to fit it in the lock. He twisted and turned, but nothing happened.

"Let me try," Amy said. She grabbed the spoon from Tom and pushed it harder. She heard a click.

"Yay, we did it!" she said. She opened the freezer and saw a lot of food in bags and boxes. She did not see any ice cream.

"Where's the ice cream?" Tom asked.

"I don't know. Maybe it's under the food," Amy said. She reached in and pulled out a bag. It had a picture of a chicken on it.

"Ew, I don't want chicken," she said. She threw the bag on the floor.

"Me neither," Tom said. He pulled out another bag. It had a picture of a fish on it.

"Ew, I don't want fish," he said. He threw the bag on the floor.

They kept pulling out bags and boxes and throwing them on the floor. They made a big mess. They did not find any ice cream.

"Where's the ice cream?" Amy asked again.

"I don't know. Maybe there's none," Tom said.

"That's not fair," Amy said. "We opened the freezer for nothing."

Just then, they heard Mommy's voice.

"Tom, Amy, what are you doing?" Mommy asked. She came into the kitchen and saw the mess. She saw the open freezer and the spoon in the lock. She was very angry.

"Tom, Amy, you are in big trouble," she said. "You broke the lock on the freezer. That was very naughty. The freezer is expensive. And you wasted all the food. That was very wasteful. And you did not find any ice cream because I hid it in the fridge. That was very smart. Now you have to clean up the mess and go to your room. No ice cream for you today."

Tom and Amy felt very sorry. They did not mean to break the lock or waste the food. They just wanted ice cream. They said sorry to Mommy and helped her clean up the mess. Then they went to their room and cried. They wished they had not opened the freezer.

Her mom said yes, and Lily was very happy.

When she finally noticed, she felt embarrassed. But then her friends told her it was okay and they all laughed and played together. From then on, Lily always made sure to be careful with her drinks, but she knew her friends would always be there for her. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a lion who lived in a jungle. He had a very bright and shiny fur. He loved to roar loudly to show his power. One day, he saw a monkey who was eating a banana. The lion asked the monkey to give him the banana, but the monkey refused. The lion got angry and started to roar at the monkey.

The monkey said, "Please don't be angry, Mr. Lion. This banana is my only food for the day. I need it to survive."

The lion realized that he was wrong to try and take the monkey's food. He said, "I'm sorry, monkey. I shouldn't have tried to take your food. Let's be friends instead."

The monkey forgave the lion and they became friends. From that day on, the lion learned to share and not to take things that didn't belong to him. The moral of the story is that it's always better to be kind and share with others, instead of being mean and selfish.

The little fish would throw the stone, and the attractive oyster would catch it with its shiny shell. They played all day, and all the other fish watched them. The little fish and the oyster became best friends, and they played together every day.

Once upon a time, there was a graceful cat named Daisy. Daisy liked to discover new things in her big backyard. One day, she found a big tree with a tip that reached the sky.

Daisy wanted to climb the tree, but she was scared. She had never gone so high before. But Daisy was brave, so she started to climb. As she went up, she saw many pretty birds and little bugs.

At the top, Daisy looked down and saw her friend, a little dog named Max. Max was barking because he was worried about Daisy. Daisy knew she had to get down to help Max feel better. She climbed down carefully, and when she reached the ground, Max was happy again. Daisy felt proud of her big adventure and was glad she could help her friend.

Once upon a time, there was a nice lady. She lived in a small house. The house was empty. The lady was sad. She wanted friends to play with.

One day, a little girl walked by the house. The lady said, "Hi! What is your name?" The little girl said, "My name is Amy! What is your name?" The lady said, "My name is Jane."

Amy and Jane became good friends. They played games and had fun. Jane's house was not empty anymore. They were both happy. And they lived happily ever after.

One day, while Fluffy was lying in the sun, she met a nice frog named Hoppy. Hoppy told Fluffy he could do a magic spell. Fluffy was very excited and wanted to see the magic.

Hoppy jumped up and down and said the magic words. Suddenly, Fluffy could jump very high, just like Hoppy! Fluffy and Hoppy played all day, jumping and laughing. They were very happy and became the best of friends.

After packing his bag, Tim went outside to play. He showed his friends his packed bag and they all thought it was great. They all played together with the equipment Tim brought. They had lots of fun and Tim was happy he packed useful things for his trip.

One day, a dog named Max went for a jog in the park. He liked to jog because it made him feel happy and strong. The sun was shining, and the grass was soft under his feet. Max saw many friends in the park, like birds, squirrels, and other dogs.

As Max jogged, he heard a tap sound. He looked around and saw a thick tree. A little bird was tapping the tree with its beak. Max stopped jogging and watched the bird tap, tap, tap the tree. The bird was making a hole in the tree to live in.

Max wanted to help the bird. So, he used his paw to tap the tree too. They worked together, tap, tap, tapping the tree. Soon, the hole was big enough for the bird to live in. The bird was very happy and thanked Max. Max felt proud and happy that he could help his friend. Then, Max continued his jog in the park, waving goodbye to the bird.

Tom and Lily were playing with their new toy car. It was red and shiny and had four big wheels. They liked to make it go fast and make loud noises.

"Vroom, vroom!" Tom said, as he pushed the car on the floor.

"Beep, beep!" Lily said, as she pretended to honk the horn.

They had a lot of fun with their toy car, until Tom had an idea.

"Let's see how high it can fly!" he said, and threw the car in the air.

"Oh no, Tom!" Lily said, "Don't do that!"

But it was too late. The car flew up and then came down with a crash. It hit the table and broke into pieces.

"Look what you did!" Lily said, "You broke our toy car!"

Tom felt bad. He saw the broken wheels and the bent door and the cracked window. He was sorry he threw the car.

"I'm sorry, Lily," he said, "I didn't mean to break it. I just wanted to see it fly."

Lily was sad and angry. She liked the toy car a lot. She didn't want to play with Tom anymore.

"Go away, Tom," she said, "You are not my friend. You are a bad boy."

Tom felt worse. He wanted to make Lily happy again. He wanted to be her friend.

"Please, Lily," he said, "Don't be mad at me. I'll fix the car. I'll glue it back together. I'll make it new again."

Lily looked at Tom. She saw that he was sorry. She saw that he wanted to help.

"Okay, Tom," she said, "But you have to be careful. You have to be gentle. You have to wait for the glue to dry."

Tom nodded. He was glad that Lily gave him a chance. He was glad that she was still his friend.

"Thank you, Lily," he said, "You are a good girl. You are a mighty friend."

They hugged and smiled. They went to get the glue and the pieces. They worked together to fix the car. They waited for the glue to dry. They hoped the car would work again. They hoped they could play with it again. They hoped they could have more fun with their toy car.

Tom and Mia liked to play pirate in the garden. They had a big box that was their ship, and they wore hats and eye patches. They pretended to sail the seas and look for treasure.

One day, they saw a big bird in the sky. It was a parrot, and it had bright colors. Tom and Mia wanted to catch the parrot and make it their pet. They thought it would be a good pirate friend.

They got some bread and put it in a cage. They hoped the parrot would come and eat the bread, and then they could close the cage. They hid behind the box and waited.

The parrot saw the bread and flew down. It was very hungry, and it liked bread. It went inside the cage and started to peck at the bread. Tom and Mia were happy and ran to the cage. They wanted to close the door and take the parrot to their ship.

But the parrot was clever and fast. It saw Tom and Mia and flew out of the cage. It flapped its wings and squawked. It was angry and scared. It did not want to be a pirate pet. It wanted to be free.

Tom and Mia were sad and sorry. They realized they had been mean to the parrot. They had tried to take it away from its home and family. They had not asked the parrot what it wanted. They had not been good pirates.

They said sorry to the parrot and let it go. They gave it the rest of the bread and some water. They watched it fly away and hoped it would be happy. They learned to be kind and respectful to animals. They decided to play pirate in a different way. They made a map and a treasure chest and had fun. They were good pirates.

It jumped at her and said, "I want to scratch you!" She was scared and ran away. Then she saw a number three that was round and fat. It rolled at her and said, "I want to squash you!" She was scared and ran away.

But she could not run fast enough. The numbers caught up with her and surrounded her. They laughed and said, "We are going to eat you!" They opened their mouths and showed their sharp teeth. Sara screamed and cried. She wanted to wake up, but she could not. She was trapped in her weird dream. The numbers moved closer and closer. Sara felt their breath on her face. Lily and Ben were playing in the park with their ball. They liked to kick the ball to each other and run after it. Sometimes they missed the ball and it rolled away. Then they had to chase it before it went too far.

One time, the ball rolled near a big dog. The dog was barking and growling. It looked angry and scary. Lily and Ben were afraid of the dog. They wanted their ball back, but they did not want to go near the dog.

"Help! Help!" they shouted. "The dog has our ball!"

A man heard them and came running. He was the dog's owner. He saw the dog and the ball and the children. He called the dog's name and told it to stop. He grabbed the dog's collar and pulled it away from the ball.

"Sorry, kids. My dog is not very friendly. He likes to protect his things. He thought the ball was his. Are you okay?" he asked.

Lily and Ben nodded. They were glad the man came. They were not hurt, but they were still scared.

"Thank you, mister. Can we have our ball back, please?" Ben asked.

"Of course. Here you go. Be careful with it. And stay away from my dog. He has a broken leg and he is in pain. That's why he is so grumpy. He needs to go to the vet soon." the man said.

He gave them the ball and walked away with his dog. Lily and Ben looked at the dog's leg. It had a bandage and a stick on it. They felt sorry for the dog. They hoped he would get better soon.

They decided to play with their ball somewhere else. They did not want to bother the dog anymore. They thanked the man again and ran to another part of the park. They had fun kicking the ball to each other and running after it. They were happy and safe.

Lila said, "Let's climb the tree and get some leaves." Tom said, "OK, but be careful. The tree is very high." They climbed the tree and picked some leaves. They put them in their pockets.

But Lila did not listen. She said, "I dare you to get that leaf. Are you scared?" Tom said, "No, I am not scared. But I am smart. It is not safe." Lila said, "You are a chicken. I will get it myself." She moved to the thin branch.

The branch cracked. Lila screamed. She fell down. She hit the ground. She hurt her head. She cried. Tom ran to her. He called for help. He was very sad. He wished Lila had listened to him. He wished they had not climbed the tree. He wished they had played something else. He wished Lila was OK.

One day, Mom and Dad let Lily and Sam make popcorn by themselves. They show them how to use the big pot and the oil and the corn. They tell them to be careful and not touch the hot things.

Lily and Sam put the oil and the corn in the pot and turn on the fire. They hear the corn start to pop. Pop, pop, pop! They see the lid of the pot move up and down. They smell the popcorn and it makes them hungry.

They want to open the pot and eat the popcorn, but Mom and Dad say not yet. They say they have to wait until the popping stops. Lily and Sam are impatient. They think the popping takes too long.

They decide to open the pot a little bit and peek inside. They think it will be fun to see the popcorn. But when they open the pot, the popcorn flies out. It goes everywhere. It lands on the floor, on the table, on the couch, on the TV, on their heads.

Lily and Sam are surprised and scared. They scream and drop the pot. Mom and Dad come running and see the mess. They are not happy. They tell Lily and Sam that they should have listened and not opened the pot.

Lily and Sam are sorry. They say they are sorry and they help Mom and Dad clean up the popcorn. They learn their lesson. They promise to never open the pot again until the popping stops. They hope they can still watch a movie and eat some popcorn.

One Sunday, Tommy has a plan. He tells his mom he has a tummy ache and he can't go to church. His mom feels his forehead and says he is not hot. She says he has to go anyway. Tommy is sad and angry.

He gets in the car with his mom and dad and his baby sister. He does not talk or smile. He looks out the window and sees the big brown building. He feels like crying. He wishes he could stay home and play with his toys.

He feels better. He smiles. He shows his picture to the other kids. They laugh. They think it is funny. They want to draw too. They take crayons and paper and start to draw their own pictures. They draw things they hate. They draw broccoli, spiders, baths, bedtime, and more.

Tommy does not listen. He does not care. He hates church. He hates the nursery teacher. He hates the story. He wishes he could go home. He looks at the clock and counts the minutes. He hopes they will not make him go to church again. He hopes. He hates. He waits.

One day, they decided to see who could build the highest tower. They each took some blocks and started to stack them on the floor. Lily used a measure to check how tall her tower was. She wanted to win the game.

Tom saw that Lily's tower was higher than his. He felt angry and jealous. He wanted to have the highest tower too. He thought of a bad idea. He sneaked behind Lily and bit her arm.

"Ow!" Lily cried. "Tom, why did you bite me? That hurts!"

Tom did not answer. He quickly grabbed some of Lily's blocks and added them to his tower. He hoped that Lily would not notice.

But Lily did notice. She saw that Tom had taken some of her blocks. She felt sad and angry. She wanted to have her blocks back. She thought of a bad idea too. She pushed Tom's tower and made it fall.

"Hey!" Tom shouted. "Lily, why did you push my tower? That's not fair!"

Lily did not answer. She took back some of her blocks and started to rebuild her tower. She hoped that Tom would not bother her again.

But Tom did bother her again. He pushed Lily's tower again and made it fall. Lily pushed Tom's tower again and made it fall. They kept pushing and biting and shouting at each other. They did not have fun anymore. They only had anger and pain.

Their teacher saw what was happening. She came over and stopped them. She asked them why they were fighting. They told her that they wanted to have the highest tower. She asked them if that was worth hurting each other. They did not know what to say.

The teacher told them that they should not bite or push or take things from each other. She told them that they should share and help and be kind to each other. She told them that they should be grateful for what they have and not be greedy for what they don't have. She told them that they should be friends and not enemies.

Lily and Tom felt sorry for what they had done. They apologized to each other and hugged. They decided to work together and build one big tower with all their blocks. They used the measure to check how tall their tower was. They were happy and proud of their tower.

But then, something bad happened. The flame grew bigger and bigger. It reached the wrapper and the tablecloth. They caught fire too. Sara got scared and dropped the match. The fire spread to the curtains and the rug. Sara screamed and ran away.

So the little bird started to sing and dance, even though she was scared. The fox was so amazed by the little bird's beautiful singing that he forgot about eating her. He even started to dance along with the little bird.

From that day on, the little bird knew that she had value and that she didn't have to be scared of anyone. She continued to sing and play on the cliff, and the fox even became her friend. The moral of the story is that even when we are scared, we should always remember our own value and never let anyone make us feel small.

Once upon a time, there was a fisherman named Tim. Tim loved to catch fish. He would go to the lake every day with his fishing rod and try to catch the biggest fish. Tim was very competitive and he wanted to catch the most fish out of all the fishermen.

One day, Tim was fishing by the lake when he saw a little boy walking by. The boy had a toy car and was playing with it. Tim waved at the boy and smiled. The boy came over and asked Tim what he was doing. Tim explained that he was trying to catch fish. The little boy was curious and wanted to help. Tim gave him a fishing rod and showed him how to rub the bait on the hook.

The little boy was excited and started to fish. Tim watched as the boy caught a fish. It was the biggest fish Tim had ever seen! Tim was amazed and proud of the little boy. From that day on, Tim and the little boy would go fishing together every day. They were no longer competitive, but instead they had fun catching fish and spending time together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the garden. One sunny day, she saw a little bug crawling on the ground. It was a tiny insect with six legs and shiny wings. She was very curious and wanted to see it up close.

Lily went closer to the insect and said, "Hello little bug! Can I play with you?" The insect didn't say anything but kept crawling. Lily picked it up gently and put it on her palm. She was grateful to the bug for letting her play with it.

Suddenly, Lily's mom called out, "Lily, it's time to go inside for lunch!" Lily knew she had to go inside, but she didn't want to leave the bug behind. So, she carefully put the insect on a leaf and said, "Goodbye little bug! I'll come back to play with you later." 

Lily went inside and had a yummy lunch. After lunch, she went back outside to play. She looked for the little bug, but it was gone. She was sad but remembered to be grateful for the fun she had playing with it earlier. From that day on, every time Lily saw an insect, she would say hello and remember her little friend.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toy cars and make them go on a track. One day, Lily's friend Tommy came over to play.

Suddenly, Lily's car stopped moving. "My car won't go," she said. 

Tommy looked at it and said, "Maybe it doesn't match the track." 

Lily looked at her car and saw that it was stuck. She tried to make it move, but it was persistent. Then, Tommy had an idea. He took his car and pushed Lily's car from behind, and it started to move again. 

"Thank you," said Lily. "You're a great friend." 

Tommy smiled and they continued to play with their cars on the track. From then on, they always made sure their cars matched the track so they wouldn't get stuck again.

Tim said to Max, "Give Spot's toy back, please." Max did not want to, but he was afraid of Tim. So, he gave the toy back to Spot. Spot was happy again. Tim told Spot, "Good job, Spot! Now, let's fold your toy and go home." Spot folded his toy, and they went home. From that day on, Max never took Spot's toy again.

Once upon a time, there was a slow turtle named Tom. Tom had a special folder where he kept his favorite pictures. He loved to look at his pictures every day.

One day, a strong wind blew Tom's folder away. Tom was sad and wanted to find his folder. He walked and walked, looking everywhere for it. He asked his friends, the birds and the squirrels, if they saw his folder.

Finally, Tom found his folder near a big tree. He was very happy! Tom decided to prevent this from happening again. He put a big rock on top of his folder so the wind could not blow it away. Now, Tom can look at his pictures every day without worrying about losing his folder.

Sara and Ben were twins who liked to play outside. One day, they saw a big pumpkin in their garden. It was orange and round and had a green stem.

"Wow, look at the pumpkin!" Sara said. "Can we pick it and make a pie?"

"Sure, let's ask Mom," Ben said. They ran to the house and found their mom in the kitchen.

"Mom, can we pick the pumpkin and make a pie?" Sara asked.

"Of course, my dears, but you have to be careful. It's very icy outside and you might slip and fall," Mom said.

"Okay, Mom, we will be careful. Thank you!" Ben said.

Sara and Ben put on their coats and boots and went back to the garden. They held hands and walked slowly to the pumpkin. They tried to lift it, but it was too heavy.

"Help, help!" Sara called. "We can't carry the pumpkin!"

Just then, they saw their neighbor, Mr. Lee, walking by. He was an old man who lived alone and liked to grow vegetables.

"Hello, Sara and Ben. Do you need some help?" Mr. Lee asked.

"Yes, please, Mr. Lee. We want to pick the pumpkin and make a pie, but it's too heavy for us," Ben said.

"No problem, I have a wheelbarrow. Let me get it and we can take the pumpkin to your house," Mr. Lee said.

He went to his garage and came back with a wheelbarrow. He put the pumpkin in it and pushed it to Sara and Ben's house. Mom opened the door and smiled.

"Thank you, Mr. Lee, for helping my children. You are very kind," Mom said.

"You're welcome, Mrs. Smith. I'm glad to help. And thank you for inviting me to share the pie with you. It smells delicious," Mr. Lee said.

Sara and Ben hugged Mr. Lee and thanked him again. They cut the pie and gave him a big slice. They ate the pie and talked and laughed. They had a good time and became friends.

The moral of the story is: Be careful when it's icy outside, and be thankful for the help of others.

"Because he is cold and needs it more than you," mom said. "You can play with other toys."

"But we love the blanket!" Ben said.

"I know, but you have to be nice to your brother. He is part of our family. How about you count how many toys you have and see how lucky you are?" mom suggested.

They looked at Sam, who was sleeping with the blanket. He looked peaceful and happy. They felt sorry for being envious of him. They decided to give him a kiss and a hug. They whispered, "We love you, Sam. And we love the blanket, too. But we can share it with you."

Lily and Ben nodded. They went to play with their other toys. They were still happy. They learned to share and to count. They loved their brother and their blanket.

Tom and Sue were friends who liked to play with toys. They had a big ship that they could sit in and pretend to sail on the water. One day, they took the ship to the park and found a pond. They wanted to put the ship in the pond and see how it floated.

"Can we do it, please?" Tom asked Sue.

"OK, but we have to be careful," Sue said. "The pond is deep and we don't have life jackets."

They carried the ship to the edge of the pond and pushed it gently. The ship floated on the water and looked very pretty. Tom and Sue smiled and clapped.

"Let's get in the ship and sail!" Tom said.

"I don't know, Tom. It looks dangerous," Sue said.

"Don't be scared, Sue. It will be fun. Come on!" Tom said.

He climbed into the ship and reached out his hand to Sue. Sue hesitated, but then took his hand and got in the ship too. They sat in the ship and pretended to steer and wave to the ducks. The ship rocked a little, but it felt peaceful and nice.

Suddenly, a big wind came and blew the ship away from the shore. Tom and Sue gasped and held on to the ship. The ship moved faster and faster on the water and spun around. Tom and Sue were scared and started to cry.

"Help! Help!" they shouted.

But no one heard them. The wind was too loud and the pond was too far. The ship hit a rock and broke into pieces. Tom and Sue fell into the water and struggled to swim. But they did not know how to swim and the water was too deep and cold. They sank under the water and did not come up again. The pond was peaceful again, but Tom and Sue were gone.

Lila and Sam were best friends. They liked to play together every day. One day, it was very cold and snowy outside. Lila and Sam wanted to have some fun in the snow.

"Let's make a snowman!" said Lila.

"OK!" said Sam. "I will show you how to make a big snowball."

They rolled and rolled the snow until they had a big snowball. Then they made another one and put it on top. They found a carrot, a hat and a scarf to make the snowman's face and clothes.

"Look at our snowman!" said Sam. "He is very funny."

"Yes, he is!" said Lila. "But I am very cold now. Let's go inside and have some cocoa."

They ran to Lila's house, where her mom was waiting for them. She smiled and gave them each a cup of hot cocoa.

"Thank you, mom!" said Lila. "This is very yummy."

"Yes, thank you!" said Sam. "This is very warm."

They drank their cocoa and felt very comfortable. They sat on the couch and watched a movie. They were very happy.

But then, something bad happened. The snowman outside was not happy. He was very angry. He did not like the carrot, the hat and the scarf. He wanted to be free. He wanted to go inside and have some cocoa too.

He broke free from the snow and started to walk towards the house. He knocked on the door with his big snowball hands.

"Who is it?" asked Lila's mom.

"It is me, the snowman!" said the snowman. "Let me in! I want some cocoa!"

Lila's mom was very scared. She did not know what to do. She tried to lock the door, but it was too late. The snowman pushed the door open and came inside. He saw Lila and Sam on the couch. He was very jealous.

"Give me your cocoa!" he shouted. "Or I will smash you!"

Lila and Sam were very scared too. They screamed and ran away. But the snowman was faster. He grabbed their cups and drank their cocoa. He spilled some on the floor and on the couch. He made a big mess.

"Ha ha ha!" he laughed. "This is my cocoa now!"

He was very happy. But Lila and Sam were not. They cried and hid behind their mom. They did not like the snowman anymore. They wished they never made him. They wished he would go away. But he did not. He stayed in the house and drank all the cocoa. He was very mean.

The end.

Sara did not like meat. She did not like how it looked, how it smelled, or how it tasted. She only liked to eat fruits, vegetables, and cheese. But her mom and dad always told her to eat some meat, too. They said it was good for her and would make her strong and healthy.

One day, mom made a big pot of stew for dinner. It had meat, potatoes, carrots, and peas in it. Mom served a bowl of stew to Sara and said, "Here you go, sweetie. Eat up and enjoy. This stew is very fine."

Sara looked at the stew and saw the chunks of meat. She felt sick. She pushed the bowl away and said, "No, thank you, mom. I do not want stew. I do not like meat. Can I have something else, please?"

Mom frowned and said, "Sara, you cannot refuse to eat what I make for you. You have to try some stew. It is not polite to say no to food. And meat is good for you. It has protein and iron and vitamins. You need them to grow and learn and play."

Sara shook her head and said, "No, mom. I do not need meat. I have protein and iron and vitamins from other foods. I eat fruits, vegetables, and cheese. They are good for me, too. And they are yummy. I do not want stew. I do not like meat. Please, mom, can I have something else?"

Mom sighed and said, "Sara, you are being very stubborn. You have to eat some meat sometimes. You cannot just eat fruits, vegetables, and cheese. You have to eat a balanced diet. That means you have to eat a little bit of everything. How about this? You eat one spoonful of stew, and then you can have some bread and butter. How does that sound?"

Sara looked at the stew again. She did not want to eat it. But she also did not want to make mom sad or angry. She wanted to be a good girl. She thought for a moment. Then she said, "OK, mom. I will eat one spoonful of stew. But only one. And then I can have some bread and butter. And maybe some grapes, too?"

Mom smiled and said, "That sounds fair, Sara. Thank you for being a good girl. Here, I will help you. I will pick a small piece of meat and some vegetables for you. You can blow on it to make it cool. Then you can eat it. It will not be so bad. You might even like it."

Sara nodded and opened her mouth. Mom put the spoonful of stew in her mouth. Sara chewed and swallowed. She did not like it. It was not yummy. But she did not spit it out. She did not cry. She did not say anything. She just made a face and drank some water.

Mom said, "Good job, Sara. You did it. You ate some stew. You ate some meat. I am proud of you. Now you can have some bread and butter. And some grapes, too. You are a very fine girl, Sara. I love you very much."

Sara smiled and said, "I love you, too, mom. Thank you for the bread and butter. And the grapes. They are yummy. But I still do not like meat. Can I have something else next time, please?"

"I know, sweetie, but you have to rest so you can get well soon. How about I read you a story?" Mommy said. She was kind and gentle.

Lily nodded. She liked stories. Mommy picked up a book and sat next to Lily. She read about a princess and a dragon and a brave knight. Lily listened and smiled. She felt a little better.

Mommy kissed Lily's forehead. "You are a good girl, Lily. I love you very much. Now, try to sleep, okay?" Mommy said.

"Okay, Mommy. I love you too. Thank you for the story," Lily said. She closed her eyes and cuddled with her teddy bear. She rested and dreamed of happy things.

Tom is a boy who likes to play with his toys. He has a lot of cars, trains, and planes that he can zoom and crash. He does not like to learn new things. He thinks they are hard and boring.

One day, his mom tells him that he has to meet a tutor. A tutor is a person who helps you learn new things. Tom does not want to meet the tutor. He wants to play with his toys. He says, "No, no, no!"

But his mom says, "Yes, yes, yes! You have to meet the tutor. He will help you read and write and count. These are important things to know. They will make you smart and healthy."

Tom does not listen. He runs to his room and grabs his favorite toy. It is a big, red fire truck. He squeezes it hard and makes a loud siren sound. He thinks, "This is my toy. I will not share it with anyone. Especially not the tutor."

But then he hears a knock on the door. It is the tutor. He is a man with glasses and a smile. He says, "Hello, Tom. I am here to help you learn new things. Can I come in and play with you?"

Tom does not answer. He squeezes his fire truck harder and makes a louder siren sound. He thinks, "Go away, go away, go away!"

But the tutor does not go away. He opens the door and walks in. He sees Tom and his fire truck. He says, "Wow, that is a nice fire truck. Can I see it?"

Tom does not want to show him. He says, "No, no, no! This is my fire truck. You cannot see it. You cannot touch it. You cannot play with it."

But the tutor is gentle and patient. He says, "Please, Tom. I just want to look at it. I like fire trucks too. They are cool and brave and helpful. They save people and animals from fires. They are heroes. Don't you want to be a hero too?"

Tom thinks for a moment. He likes heroes. He likes to save people and animals. He likes to be cool and brave and helpful. He looks at the tutor and sees his glasses and his smile. He thinks, "Maybe he is not so bad. Maybe he can help me learn new things. Maybe he can be my friend."

He loosens his grip on his fire truck and says, "Okay, okay, okay. You can see my fire truck. But you have to be careful. It is my favorite toy."

The tutor says, "Thank you, Tom. I will be careful. I promise. And I will also teach you how to read and write and count. These are fun and easy things to learn. They will make you smarter and healthier. And they will also make you a better hero."

Tom smiles and says, "Okay, okay, okay. Let's learn new things. But first, let's play with my fire truck."

The tutor smiles and says, "Okay, okay, okay. Let's play with your fire truck. And then, let's learn new things."

They play and learn together. They have fun and become friends. Tom is happy. He likes his fire truck. He likes his tutor. He likes to learn new things. He thinks, "This is a good day."

"I feel better now," said Lily.

"Goodnight," said her teddy bear.

And she fell asleep.

The moral of the story is that it's important to take care of ourselves and others, especially when it's wet and cold outside.

But then, the bunny realized that its leg was stuck in the trap. It couldn't hop away. The bunny was scared and alone. It wished it had never tried to get the carrot. The trap was unique and very strong. The bunny couldn't escape.

The bunny's friends searched and searched for it, but they couldn't find it. The bunny was trapped forever. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toy car. His car was red and shiny. One day, Timmy's car stopped moving. He looked at the car and saw that the battery was empty. 

Timmy went to his mom and said, "Mommy, my car needs a new battery." His mom said, "Let's go to the store and get a new one." So, they went to the store and bought a new battery. 

When they got home, Timmy put the new battery in his car and drove it to the park. He loved to play with his car in the park. But, while he was playing, a big dog came and took his car. Timmy was sad because he loved his car. 

Timmy went home and told his mom what happened. His mom said, "Don't worry, we will get you a new car." Timmy was happy because he knew his mom would always help him. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a bunny named Benny. Benny was very grumpy because he lost his veil. He asked his friend, the bird, "Have you seen my veil?" The bird replied, "No, I haven't seen it. But I can help you find it!"

Benny and the bird hopped around the garden, looking for the veil. They looked under the flowers and behind the bushes. Suddenly, they saw a gust of wind blow the veil away. Benny and the bird chased after it until they finally caught it.

Benny was very happy to have his veil back. He thanked his friend and said, "I'm sorry for being grumpy earlier. You're a good friend." The bird smiled and said, "That's what friends are for!" From that day on, Benny and the bird were the best of friends and they hopped around the garden together every day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to dance. She would twirl and jump and spin around her room every day. One day, Lily noticed an itch on her arm. She scratched and scratched, but the itch wouldn't go away.

Days passed, and Lily started feeling very tired. She didn't want to dance anymore, and her face became pale. Her mom took her to the doctor, who said Lily had a bad case of the chickenpox. Lily had to stay in bed for a whole week, and she couldn't dance or play with her friends.

Finally, the day came when Lily felt better. She was so happy to be healthy again that she started to dance right away. She twirled and jumped and spun around her room, and she felt so good that she forgot all about the itchy chickenpox. From then on, Lily danced every day and never took her health for granted again.

As they walked, Spot saw a bird and tried to chase it. Suddenly, he felt a tug on his collar. "No, Spot," his owner said. "You can't chase the bird. You might get lost." Spot was sad, but he understood.

After their walk, Spot went to sleep. But in the middle of the night, he woke up and barked. "What's wrong, Spot?" his owner asked. Spot barked again and his owner realized that he had forgotten to take off Spot's collar. "Sorry, Spot," his owner said as he took off the collar. "Goodnight, little dog." Spot wagged his tail and went back to sleep, happy and collar-free.

Jenny looked at the diary and said, "Yes, I want to read it with you. But first, let's share it. You can read the first page and I'll read the second page."

Timmy agreed and they took turns reading the diary. They found out it belonged to a girl named Sarah and she wrote about her bitter feelings. Timmy and Jenny didn't understand what bitter meant, so they asked their mom.

Their mom explained that bitter meant feeling sad and angry at the same time. Timmy and Jenny felt bad for Sarah and decided to write a nice note in her diary to make her feel better.

"Dear Sarah, we read your diary and we want you to know that we are your friends. We hope you feel better soon. Love, Timmy and Jenny." 

They shared the diary and their kindness with Sarah, and it made them all happy. The end.

After the race, Lily and her family went to a park. There were lots of people there and everyone was busy. Some people were playing games, some were eating food, and some were just sitting and talking. Lily played with her friends and had lots of fun. She was very busy too!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a charming smile and loved to play in the park. One day, she decided to wander around the park and explore. As she was walking, she found a leather ball lying on the ground. It was a beautiful brown color and felt smooth to the touch. 

Lily picked up the ball and started to play with it. She bounced it up and down and kicked it around. Suddenly, a group of children came over and asked if they could play too. Lily was happy to share and they all played together with the leather ball. 

After a while, it was time for Lily to go home. She said goodbye to her new friends and walked back home with the leather ball in her hand. When she got home, she showed her mom the charming leather ball she found in the park. Her mom smiled and said it was a great find. Lily was happy and went to bed dreaming of all the fun she would have with her new ball. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily and her mom went to the market. Lily saw lots of fruits and vegetables there. She asked her mom, "What is this?" Her mom replied, "This is a tomato."

Lily was curious and asked her mom, "Can you teach me how to cook with tomatoes?" Her mom smiled and said, "Of course, I can teach you how to make tomato sauce."

As they walked through the market, they saw a mysterious man selling colorful stones. Lily asked her mom, "Who is that man?" Her mom said, "He is a seller. He sells stones that are very pretty."

Lily was fascinated by the stones and asked the man, "Can you teach me how to find these stones?" The man smiled and said, "Yes, I can teach you how to find them in the river." Lily was very happy and thanked the man.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She lived in a house with a big door. One day, Lily's mom went out to buy groceries and told her to remain inside the house. Lily played with her toys and waited for her mom to come back. 

Suddenly, she heard a loud noise outside the door. She got scared and ran to hide under the bed. After a while, she peeked out from under the bed and saw that it was just the postman delivering a package. Lily felt grateful that it wasn't something scary.

When her mom came back, Lily told her about the noise and how she remained hidden under the bed. Her mom hugged her and said she was grateful that Lily was safe. From that day on, Lily made sure to always lock the door when her mom went out.

Once upon a time, there was a big man. He had a pistol that was very heavy. One day, he went for a walk in the forest. He heard a noise and looked around. He saw a little rabbit. The rabbit was scared and ran away. The man felt bad for scaring the rabbit and put his heavy pistol away. From that day on, he promised to be kind to all the animals in the forest.

Once upon a time, there was a famous superhero named Lightning. One day, Lightning's archenemy, a mean villain, stole something very important from Lightning's city. Lightning knew he had to stop the villain and get the thing back. 

So, Lightning sent a message to all his superhero friends for help. They all came together to make a plan to catch the villain. They decided to use Lightning's super-fast speed to chase after the villain. 

After a long chase, they finally caught the villain and got the important thing back. Lightning and his friends celebrated their victory with a big party. Everyone was happy and Lightning became even more famous for saving the day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily had a brother named Max who was very sweet. They loved to play together and have fun. One day, Max went to visit his grandma and Lily missed him so much. She waited and waited for him to come home but he didn't. 

Lily asked her mom where Max was and her mom told her that he was still at grandma's house. Lily felt sad because she wanted to play with her sweet brother. She decided to draw a picture for him to show how much she missed him. 

A few days later, Max came back from grandma's house and Lily was so happy to see him. She gave him the picture and he loved it. They hugged each other and played together again. Lily was happy to have her sweet brother back home.

Anna wanted to watch TV. She liked the show with the pink pig and the funny duck. But her brother Ben was watching something else. He liked the show with the big cars and the loud noises. Anna asked him to change the channel, but he said no. He said he was older and he could choose.

Anna was sad. She sighed. She looked for something else to do. She saw her toys on the floor. She had a doll, a ball, a puzzle, and a book. But she did not want to play with them. She wanted to watch TV.

She went to her mom. She said, "Mom, can I watch TV? Ben is watching something else. I don't like it." Her mom smiled. She said, "I'm sorry, Anna. But there is only one TV in the house. And Ben has the remote. You have to wait your turn. Why don't you play with your toys? They are available. They are fun."

Anna sighed again. She did not think her toys were fun. She thought they were boring. She went back to her room. She sat on her bed. She looked at the wall. She wished she had another TV. Or another brother.

Ben and Lily were playing in the garden. They had a big box that they pretended was a car. They took turns driving and honking.

"Beep beep! Where are we going, Lily?" Ben asked.

"We are going to the market, Ben. We need to buy some carrots for our soup," Lily said.

"Carrots? I don't like carrots. They are not yummy," Ben said.

"Yes, they are, Ben. They are good for you. They make your eyes bright and your teeth strong," Lily said.

They arrived at the market and got out of the box. They saw a stall with many vegetables. They saw red tomatoes, green cucumbers, yellow corn, and orange carrots.

"Look, Ben, there are the carrots. Let's get some," Lily said.

She picked up a bunch of carrots and gave them to Ben.

"Here, Ben, you hold these. They are not heavy," she said.

Ben took the carrots and felt them. They were smooth and hard. He smelled them. They had a sweet and earthy smell.

"Maybe they are not so bad," he thought.

They paid the seller and got back in the box. They drove home and gave the carrots to their mom.

"Thank you, Ben and Lily. You are such good helpers. I will make a yummy soup with these carrots. Do you want to help me?" their mom asked.

"Yes, please, mom. We want to help," Ben and Lily said.

They washed the carrots and peeled them. They cut them into small pieces and put them in a pot with water and salt. They added some onion, garlic, and parsley. They stirred the soup and waited for it to boil.

"Wow, it smells good, mom. Can we taste it?" Ben asked.

"Sure, Ben. But be careful, it's hot. Blow on it first," their mom said.

She gave them each a spoonful of soup. They blew on it and tasted it.

"Mmm, it's yummy, mom. I like it," Lily said.

"Me too, mom. It's yummy. I like carrots now," Ben said.

They smiled and hugged their mom. They enjoyed their soup and ate all the carrots. They were happy and full.

Anna was sad. She did not have any friends to play with. She looked out the window and saw the cold snow. She wanted to go outside and make a snowman, but she had no one to help her.

She put on her coat and boots and went to the yard. She saw a big pile of snow. She started to pick up some snow and roll it into a ball. She made a big ball for the snowman's body. Then she made a smaller ball for the head. She put the head on top of the body.

She looked for something to make the snowman's face. She saw a carrot on the ground. She picked it up and stuck it in the snowman's head for a nose. She found two rocks and used them for eyes. She found a stick and used it for a mouth. She smiled at her snowman. He looked funny.

She heard a voice behind her. "Hi, can I play with you?" She turned around and saw a boy from her street. He had a hat and a scarf and gloves. He looked friendly.

"Hi, I'm Anna. This is my snowman. Do you want to help me make him a hat?" she asked.

"Sure, I'm Ben. I like your snowman. He has a nice nose. Can we use this pine cone for a hat?" he said.

They picked up the pine cone and put it on the snowman's head. They laughed. They made the snowman a scarf out of some leaves. They gave him some arms out of some twigs. They hugged their snowman.

Anna was not sad anymore. She had a new friend to play with. She liked the cold snow. She was happy.

Ben and Lily are playing with their toy cars in the living room. They like to make them zoom and crash on the carpet. Ben has a red car and Lily has a blue car. They pretend that their cars have power and can do anything.

"Look, my car can jump over the sofa!" Ben says, and makes his car fly in the air.

"No, it can't! My car is faster and stronger!" Lily says, and chases Ben's car with her car.

They start to argue and bump their cars into each other. They make loud noises and angry faces.

"Stop it, you two!" Mom says, coming into the room. "You are making too much noise and you are not sharing. You need to play nicely or I will take away your cars."

Ben and Lily stop and look at Mom. They don't want to lose their cars. They like their cars.

"Sorry, Mom," Ben says.

"Sorry, Mom," Lily says.

Mom smiles and says, "That's better. Why don't you try to play a different game with your cars? Maybe you can make them go on an adventure or help someone in trouble."

Ben and Lily think for a moment. They like the idea of an adventure. They decide to make their cars go on a mission to find a hidden treasure. They use a pillow as a mountain, a blanket as a river, and a book as a map. They make their cars work together and have fun.

"Look, we found the treasure!" Ben says, opening a box of cookies.

"Yay, we did it!" Lily says, taking a cookie.

They share the cookies and the power of their cars. They are happy and Mom is proud.

Lily and her mom were going to the airport. They had big bags and a small cat. Lily was anxious. She did not like flying. She did not like loud noises. She did not like strangers.

"Mom, can we stay home?" Lily asked.

"No, sweetie, we have to go. We are going to see grandma and grandpa. They miss you very much. And you will like the plane. It is like a big bird. It will take us high in the sky," mom said.

Lily was not sure. She held her cat tight. She looked out the window. She saw cars and buses and trucks. She saw people and signs and lights. She saw the airport. It was huge. It had many planes. Some were white, some were blue, some were red. Some were taking off, some were landing, some were waiting.

"Look, Lily, there is our plane. It is blue and yellow. It has a smiley face on the tail. Do you see it?" mom said.

Lily saw it. It was big and bright. It did have a smiley face. Lily smiled too. Maybe the plane was friendly. Maybe it would not be scary.

They got out of the car. They took their bags and their cat. They walked to the airport. They showed their tickets and their passports. They put their bags on a belt. They went through a gate. They followed a lady. She took them to the plane.

"Hello, welcome aboard. What is your name?" the lady asked Lily.

"Lily," Lily said.

"What a lovely name. And who is this?" the lady asked, pointing to the cat.

"This is Fluffy. He is my best friend," Lily said.

"He is very cute. Do you know what? He can sit with you on the plane. He has a special seat. Do you want to see it?" the lady asked.

Lily nodded. She was curious. The lady showed her a small cage. It had a blanket and a bowl. It had a window and a door. It had a tag that said "Fluffy".

"This is Fluffy's seat. He can see you and you can see him. He can drink water and eat food. He can sleep and play. He will be very comfortable. Do you want to put him in?" the lady asked.

Lily hesitated. She did not want to leave Fluffy. She wanted to hold him. But she saw that the cage was nice. She saw that Fluffy would be safe. She saw that the lady was kind.

"OK," Lily said. She kissed Fluffy and said "I love you". She opened the door and put him in. She closed the door and locked it. She poured some water in the bowl. She gave him a toy. She said "Be good".

Fluffy meowed. He licked Lily's hand. He looked at her with big eyes. He said "I love you too".

Lily smiled. She felt better. She took her mom's hand. They walked to their seats. They buckled their belts. They listened to the pilot. He said "Welcome aboard. We are ready to fly. Have a nice trip".

Lily looked at Fluffy. He looked at her. They waved. They were ready to fly. They were not anxious anymore. They were excited. They were going to see grandma and grandpa. They were going to have fun.

Tom and Lily are twins. They like to go to the mall with Mom. The mall has many shops and toys and people. Tom and Lily want to see everything.

One day, Mom says, "Stay with me, please. The mall is big and busy. Do not run away." Tom and Lily nod. They follow Mom to the book shop. Mom looks at books. Tom and Lily look at books too. They see a book with a big red car. They want the book.

But Mom says, "No, we have enough books at home. Let's go to another shop." Tom and Lily are sad. They do not want to go. They want the book. They see Mom walk away. They have an idea. They run to the book and grab it. They hide behind a shelf. They think Mom will not see them.

But Mom sees them. She is angry and scared. She says, "Tom and Lily, come here now! You are naughty and silly. You cannot take things that are not yours. You could get lost or hurt. You have to follow me and listen to me. That is the rule. I love you and I want you to be safe."

Tom and Lily are sorry. They drop the book and run to Mom. They hug her and say, "We are sorry, Mom. We love you too. We will follow you and listen to you. We do not need the book. We have each other."

Mom smiles and hugs them back. She says, "Thank you, Tom and Lily. You are good and smart. You learned a lesson today. The mall is fun, but it is not a regular place. You have to be careful and respectful. You have to follow the rules. That is how you can enjoy the mall and be happy."

Sara and Tom were twins who lived near the sea. They liked to play on the sand and look at the boats. One day, they saw a big boat with many flags and people. They wondered who was on the boat and what they were doing.

"Let's go and see the boat," Tom said. "Maybe they have toys and candy."

"But we are not allowed to go near the water," Sara said. "Mom and Dad said it is dangerous."

"Please, Sara, just for a little bit," Tom begged. "We will be careful and not go too close."

Sara was scared, but she did not want to make Tom sad. She agreed to go with him, but she held his hand tightly. They walked along the shore until they reached the boat. They saw a man with a hat and a coat on the deck. He looked wealthy and important.

"Hello, children," the man said. "What are you doing here?"

"We just wanted to see your boat," Tom said. "It is very nice and big."

"Thank you," the man said. "This is my boat. I travel around the world and see many things. Do you like the sea?"

"Yes, we do," Sara said. "But we are not supposed to be here. We have to go back to our home."

The man smiled and gave them each a shiny coin. "Here, take these as a gift. They are from a faraway land. But you are right, you should not stay here too long. The sea can be dangerous and you need to listen to your parents. They love you and want you to be safe."

"Thank you, sir," Tom and Sara said. They put the coins in their pockets and ran back to their home. They told their parents about the boat and the man and showed them the coins. Their parents were surprised and happy, but also a little angry.

"We are glad you met a nice man and got a gift, but you should never go near the water without us," their mom said. "The sea can be fun, but also scary. You could get hurt or lost."

"We are sorry, Mom and Dad," Tom and Sara said. "We will not do it again. We love you and the sea."

They hugged their parents and went to bed. They dreamed of the boat and the man and the coins. They wondered what other things the man had seen and where he was going next. They hoped to see him again someday.

She tries to grab the truck from Ben, but he holds on tight. They pull and tug and fight over the truck. Then they hear a loud snap. The truck breaks in half. Anna and Ben stop and look at the broken truck. They feel sad and sorry.

"Look what you did. You broke my truck. It was my favorite toy," Ben says.

"I'm sorry, Ben. I didn't mean to break it. I was just being bossy. Can you forgive me?" Anna says.

Ben thinks for a moment. He is still angry, but he also loves his sister. He decides to be kind and share.
