Anna smiles and hugs Ben. She is happy that he is not mad at her. She takes his half of the truck and they play together on the carpet. They learn to be nice and take turns. They have fun with their toys.

Tom and Lily were playing in the park. They liked to swing, slide and run. They saw a chubby dog with a red collar. The dog was barking and wagging its tail.

"Can we pet the dog?" Lily asked Tom.

"OK, but be careful. He might bite," Tom said.

They walked slowly to the dog. The dog ran to them and licked their faces. He was very friendly. Tom and Lily laughed and hugged the dog.

"Hello, doggy. What is your name?" Lily said.

The dog barked again. He seemed to say, "My name is Spot."

Tom and Lily realized that the dog was lost. He had no owner. They looked around and saw a sign on a tree. The sign had a picture of the dog and some words.

"Look, Lily. The sign says that Spot is missing. Someone is looking for him," Tom said.

They read the phone number on the sign. They decided to call the number and tell them where Spot was.

They found a phone near the park. They dialed the number and waited.

"Hello?" a voice said.

"Hello, we found Spot. He is in the park. He is a chubby dog with a red collar. He is very nice," Tom said.

"Spot? You found Spot? Oh, thank you, thank you. We have been looking for him for days. He ran away from home. We miss him so much. Where are you? We will come and get him right away," the voice said.

Tom told them where they were. They waited for Spot's owner to come. They played with Spot and gave him some water. They saw a car stop near the park. A man and a woman got out of the car. They looked happy and worried.

"Spot! Spot! There you are. We are so glad you are safe. Thank you, kids, for finding him. You are very kind," the man said.

He hugged Spot and put him in the car. The woman gave Tom and Lily a hug and a cookie. She thanked them again.

"Bye, Spot. We are happy you found your home. We hope to see you again," Lily said.

"Bye, kids. You are the best. We will never forget you," Spot barked.

Tom and Lily waved goodbye to Spot and his owners. They felt good. They had helped a friend. They went back to the park and continued to play. They saw a motion in the bushes. They wondered what it was. Maybe another animal. Maybe another adventure.

Sara and Tom were playing in the snow. They saw a big reindeer with a red nose. The reindeer was pulling a sled with many colorful boxes.

"Wow, look at that!" Sara said. "It is so pretty!"

"Maybe it is Santa's reindeer," Tom said. "Do you think he has gifts for us?"

"I don't know," Sara said. "But I want to see."

She ran towards the reindeer. Tom followed her.

"Wait, Sara!" Tom said. "Don't go too close. It might be scary."

Sara did not listen. She wanted to touch the reindeer. She reached out her hand.

"Hello, reindeer," she said. "You are so soft and warm."

The reindeer looked at her and smiled. He did not mind. He liked Sara.

"Hi, little girl," he said. "You are very brave. Do you want to ride on my sled?"

Sara was surprised. The reindeer could talk!

"Yes, please!" she said. "That would be fun!"

She climbed on the sled. Tom was still afraid.

"Sara, come back!" he said. "You don't know him. He might take you away."

Sara shook her head.

"No, Tom," she said. "He is nice. He is my friend. Don't be scared. Come with me."

She held out her hand. Tom hesitated. He wanted to be brave too. He wanted to see the colorful boxes.

He took a deep breath. He dared to take Sara's hand. He joined her on the sled.

The reindeer laughed.

"Good boy," he said. "You are brave too. Now, hold on tight. We are going for a ride."

He gave a loud snort. He ran fast. The sled flew in the air. Sara and Tom squealed with joy. They saw the snow and the trees and the stars. They felt the wind and the cold and the warmth. They had the best time ever. They thanked the reindeer for the ride.

The reindeer smiled.

"You are welcome," he said. "You are very good children. I have a gift for each of you."

He gave them each a colorful box. Sara and Tom opened them. They found toys and books and candy. They hugged the reindeer.

"Thank you, thank you, thank you!" they said. "You are the best reindeer ever!"

The reindeer winked.

"You are welcome, welcome, welcome!" he said. "You are the best children ever! Merry Christmas!"

He waved goodbye. He flew away. Sara and Tom waved back. They ran home. They told their mom and dad about their adventure. They showed them their gifts. They were very happy. They never forgot the reindeer with the red nose. He never forgot them either.

CRASH!

"Ben and Lily, you are foolish!" Mom said. "You should not rock the melon. It is for eating, not for playing. And you should not break the fence. It is for keeping us safe, not for crashing. You are in trouble!"

Lily likes to polish her shoes. She uses a soft cloth and some shiny stuff. She rubs her shoes until they look new. She is very proud of her shoes.

One morning, she is polishing her shoes in the kitchen. Her mom is making toast for breakfast. She smells the toast and feels hungry.

"Mom, can I have some toast?" she asks.

"Sure, honey. Here you go." Her mom gives her a plate with two slices of toast. One has butter and jam, the other has cheese and ham.

Lily takes a bite of the cheese and ham toast. She makes a face. The toast is rough and dry. She does not like it.

"Mom, this toast is rough. I don't want it." She pushes the plate away.

Her mom looks at the toast. She sees that it is burnt. She forgot to check the toaster.

"Oh, I'm sorry, Lily. I made a mistake. The toaster was too hot. Let me make you another one." She takes the plate and puts it in the trash.

She makes a new toast for Lily. This one is soft and golden. She puts butter and jam on it.

"Here, try this one. It's much better." She gives Lily the new toast.

Lily takes a bite of the butter and jam toast. She smiles. The toast is sweet and yummy. She likes it.

"Thank you, mom. This toast is good. I love you." She hugs her mom.

"I love you too, Lily. And I love your shoes. They are so shiny." Her mom hugs her back.

They eat their toast and talk about their day. Lily is happy. She has a good mom and a good toast. And she has the best shoes in the world.

One day, a big dog came to the park. It saw the toy cars and wanted to play with them. It ran towards Tom and Lily and barked loudly. Tom and Lily were scared. They did not want the dog to take their toy cars.

"Help, help!" they shouted. "Go away, dog!"

But the dog did not listen. It grabbed one of the toy cars in its mouth and ran away. Tom and Lily chased after it, but it was too fast. They felt sad and angry.

Then they saw a man on a bike. He was wearing a hat and a badge. He was a police officer. He heard Tom and Lily's cries and saw the dog with the toy car.

"Stop, dog!" he said. "Give back the toy car!"

He rode his bike after the dog and blew his whistle. The dog was scared of the whistle and dropped the toy car. The police officer picked it up and gave it back to Tom and Lily.

"Thank you, thank you!" they said. "You are very helpful!"

The police officer smiled and patted their heads.

"You're welcome, kids. I'm glad I could help. Be careful with your toy cars. They are not for dogs."

Tom and Lily nodded and hugged their toy cars. They were happy to have them back. They thanked the police officer again and went back to the park. They continued to play and drive their toy cars, but they kept an eye on the dog. They did not want to escape again.

Jen and Sam like to play in the park. They run and jump and slide on the grass. They see a big round thing that can spin. They want to try it.

"Can we go on the spinny thing?" Jen asks Sam.

"Yes, let's go!" Sam says. They run to the spinny thing and sit on it. They hold on tight and push with their feet. The spinny thing goes faster and faster. Jen and Sam feel the wind on their faces. They laugh and scream.

"Wow, this is fun!" Jen says.

"I like to spin!" Sam says.

But then the spinny thing goes too fast. Jen and Sam feel dizzy. They let go of the spinny thing and fly off. They land on the grass. They roll and tumble. They stop and look at each other.

"Are you okay?" Jen asks Sam.

"I'm okay. Are you okay?" Sam asks Jen.

They nod and smile. They are glad they are not hurt. They stand up and dust off their clothes. They hug each other.

"That was scary!" Jen says.

"But also fun!" Sam says.

They decide to play something else. They run to the swings and swing high and low. They forget about the spinny thing. They are happy.

Tom and Lily were playing outside in the garden. They liked to run, jump and laugh. They saw many things: flowers, birds, bugs and a big sun.

"Look, Lily, the sun is so bright and warm!" Tom said.

"Yes, Tom, I like the sun. It makes me happy!" Lily said.

They played some more, but then they saw something in the sky. It was a cloud. A big, gray cloud. It was not bright and warm like the sun. It was dark and cold.

"Tom, what is that?" Lily asked.

"That is a cloud, Lily. Sometimes clouds appear in the sky. They are made of water and air." Tom said.

"Water and air? But why is it gray?" Lily asked.

"Because it has a lot of water inside. Sometimes, when clouds have too much water, they rain. Rain is when water falls from the sky." Tom said.

"Rain? I don't like rain. It makes me wet and sad!" Lily said.

"Don't worry, Lily. Rain is not bad. It helps the flowers, the birds and the bugs. And sometimes, after the rain, you can see a rainbow. A rainbow is when the sun makes many colors in the sky." Tom said.

"Really? A rainbow? I like colors. They make me happy!" Lily said.

"Then let's go inside and wait for the rain to stop. Maybe we will see a rainbow later." Tom said.

"OK, Tom. Let's go. But can we play some more after the rain?" Lily asked.

"Of course, Lily. We can play as much as we want. We are friends!" Tom said.

They held hands and ran inside. They hoped to see a rainbow soon. They liked to play outside in the garden. They liked to see many things: flowers, birds, bugs and a big sun. And sometimes, a cloud. A big, gray cloud.

Tom and Sam were brothers who liked to play in the bathroom. They pretended to be pirates and explorers, and used the towels and soap as their treasure and tools. One day, they found a shiny thing on the sink that they had never seen before. It looked like a knife, but with many teeth.

"What is this?" Tom asked, picking it up.

"I don't know. Let me see." Sam said, reaching for it.

Tom did not want to share. He wanted to examine the shiny thing by himself. He ran away from Sam and locked the door.

"Tom, open the door! That's not a toy! That's a razor!" Sam shouted, banging on the door.

Tom did not listen. He was curious about the razor. He touched the teeth with his finger. They felt sharp and cold. He wondered what they could do. He looked at his face in the mirror. He saw his hair and his nose and his mouth. He thought he looked wild, like a lion. He wanted to look more wild. He had an idea. He put the razor on his hair and pulled it down.

"Ow!" Tom screamed. He felt a pain on his head. He saw blood on the razor and on his hair. He dropped the razor and started to cry.

Sam heard Tom's scream and kicked the door open. He saw Tom holding his head and bleeding. He saw the razor and the hair on the sink. He was scared and angry.

"Tom, what did you do? You hurt yourself with the razor! You are silly and naughty!" Sam yelled.

He ran to Tom and hugged him. He tried to stop the blood with a towel. He called for their mom.

Mom came and saw what happened. She was shocked and worried. She took Tom to the hospital. She scolded Sam for leaving the razor on the sink. She told them to never play with razors again. They were dangerous and not for children.

Tom and Sam learned their lesson. They felt sorry and ashamed. They said sorry to mom and to each other. They promised to be careful and to share their toys. They never played with razors again.

Lily and Ben were best friends. They liked to play together, share toys and help each other. One day, they found a shiny ring in the park. It was very pretty and sparkled in the sun.

"Look, Lily, I found a ring!" Ben said, holding it up.

"Wow, it's so nice!" Lily said, admiring it.

"Let's play a game. I will be the prince and you will be the princess. I will give you the ring and ask you to marry me. Then you will say yes and we will be happy," Ben suggested.

"OK, that sounds fun," Lily agreed.

They went to a quiet spot under a big tree. Ben knelt down and held out the ring to Lily.

"Lily, you are my best friend and I love you very much. Will you marry me?" Ben asked.

Lily looked at the ring and at Ben. She felt happy and scared at the same time. She did not know what marriage meant, but she knew it was something important and special. She wanted to make Ben happy, but she also wondered what would happen next.

"Ben, I love you too and you are my best friend. But what is marriage? What do we do if we marry?" Lily asked.

Ben thought for a moment. He did not know much about marriage either, but he had seen his parents and other grown-ups do it.

"Marriage is when two people love each other and want to be together forever. They wear rings and say nice words and kiss and hug. They also live in the same house and share everything and take care of each other. They are happy and sometimes they have children," Ben explained.

Lily nodded. She liked the idea of being with Ben forever and doing nice things with him. She also liked the idea of having children, like her baby brother. She smiled and took the ring from Ben.

"OK, Ben, I will marry you. You are my prince and I am your princess. We will be happy and have children," Lily said.

Ben smiled and put the ring on Lily's finger. They hugged and kissed and said nice words. They felt very happy and proud. They did not notice that their parents were watching them from a distance, smiling and laughing. They had seen the whole thing and thought it was very cute and sweet. They decided to let them play and enjoy their game, knowing that they were too young to understand what marriage really meant. They hoped that they would always be friends and love each other, no matter what.

"I don't know, Tom," Lily said. "Maybe someone nice. Maybe they will provide us with some food or toys."

"Yes, please!" Lily said. "That sounds fun!"

Once upon a time, in a big forest, there lived a healthy little mosquito named Buzz. Buzz loved to fly around and play with his friends. One day, Buzz met a new friend named Bee. Bee was very good at making sounds with her wings.

"Sure," said Bee, "I like making sounds. Let's play together."

So, Buzz and Bee played all day. Buzz recorded the sounds of Bee's wings, and they had lots of fun. They also made friends with other animals in the forest. Everyone liked the sounds they made together.

At the end of the day, Buzz and Bee were tired but happy. They had made many new friends and had a great time playing together. Buzz was glad he had recorded the sounds, so he could listen to them whenever he wanted. Buzz and Bee knew they would be best friends forever.

Bob felt sad but still wanted to make Fred happy. He hopped around Fred and tried to make him laugh. But the more Bob hopped, the grumpier Fred became.

Then, Fred got very angry and said, "Stop hopping, Bob! I don't like it!" Bob didn't listen and kept hopping. Fred got so mad that he hopped away, leaving Bob all alone.

In the end, Bob was sad because he couldn't make Fred happy. He hopped back home, feeling very upset.

"What does 'harm' mean, Mama?" asked Lily. 

"It means to hurt something or someone," explained her mom.

Lily's mom shook her head. "I'm sorry, I don't," she said. 

The man sighed. "I need to change a law that's causing harm to my clients," he said. 

Lily didn't understand what he meant, but she knew that the man needed help. "Mama, can we help him?" she asked. 

Her mom smiled. "Of course, we can try," she said. 

And so, Lily and her mom helped the man find a lawyer who could change the law and make things better for his clients. The butterfly flew away, and Lily felt happy knowing that they had done something good.

Anna and Ben were playing in the kitchen. They saw a big knife on the table. It was shiny and sharp.

"Look, a knife!" Ben said. "I want to touch it."

"No, Ben, no!" Anna said. "The knife is not for playing. It can hurt you. Mommy said so."

Anna tried to explain to Ben why the knife was dangerous, but Ben did not listen. He reached for the knife with his hand.

"Ben, stop!" Anna shouted. She grabbed his arm and pulled him away from the knife. The knife fell on the floor with a loud clang.

Mommy heard the noise and came into the kitchen. She saw the knife on the floor and Anna and Ben looking scared.

"What happened here?" Mommy asked. She was angry and worried.

"Mommy, I'm sorry!" Anna said. "Ben wanted to touch the knife, but I stopped him. I tried to explain, but he did not listen."

Mommy picked up the knife and put it back on the table. She hugged Anna and Ben and said, "Thank you, Anna, for being a good sister and protecting Ben. Ben, you have to listen to Anna and me. The knife is not a toy. It can cut you and make you bleed. Do you understand?"

Ben nodded his head and said, "Yes, Mommy, I understand. I'm sorry, too."

Mommy smiled and said, "It's okay, Ben. I'm glad you're okay. Now, let's tidy up the kitchen and then we can have some cookies."

But the fish was not happy. It was scared and it flopped in the net. It wanted to go back to the pond. Lily saw the fish and felt sorry for it. She said, "Ben, the fish is sad. You should release it."

Ben did not want to release the fish. He wanted to keep it and play with it. He said, "No, Lily, the fish is mine. I caught it. It is fun."

Mom saw that Lily and Ben were arguing. She said, "Ben, Lily is right. The fish belongs in the pond. It is not good to keep it in the net. It will die. You should release it and say sorry to the fish."

Ben looked at the fish and saw that it was not moving much. He realized that Mom and Lily were right. He felt bad and said, "Okay, Mom, Lily, I will release the fish. I am sorry, fish."

He gently put the net back in the water and let the fish go. The fish swam away and joined the other fish. Ben said, "Bye, fish. Have a good day."

Lily smiled and hugged Ben. She said, "Good job, Ben. You are a good brother."

Mom smiled and hugged them both. She said, "I am proud of you, Ben and Lily. You are good children. Now, let's go and have some ice cream."

Lily and Tom were playing in the backyard. They liked to pretend they were mail people. They had a big box of old papers and envelopes. They wrote their names and drew pictures on them. Then they put them in their bags and went to deliver them to their friends.

They knocked on the door of Sam's house. Sam opened the door and smiled. "Hi, Lily and Tom! Do you have mail for me?" he asked.

"Yes, we do!" Lily said. She gave him an envelope with a sticker of a fire truck on it. "This is for you, Sam. It is from the fire people. They say you are very brave and good."

"Wow, thank you, Lily and Tom! That is so nice of them. And of you!" Sam said. He opened the envelope and looked at the paper inside. It had a big fire on it, with red and orange and yellow crayons. He liked fire. It was bright and warm and made noises.

"Can I show you something?" Sam asked. He took Lily and Tom to his backyard. There was a small fire pit there, with some sticks and rocks. "My dad made this for me. He said we can make a fire sometimes, but only when he is here. And we have to be careful and not touch it. Do you want to see?"

"Yes, please!" Lily and Tom said. They followed Sam to the fire pit. Sam took a match from a box and struck it on the side. It made a spark and a flame. He put it on the sticks and they caught fire. The fire grew bigger and bigger. It was beautiful.

Lily and Tom clapped their hands and cheered. "Wow, Sam, you are so good at making fire!" Lily said.

"Thank you, Lily. It is fun. But we have to be safe. We have to stay away from the fire and not throw anything in it. And we have to put it out when we are done. Do you know how to put out a fire?" Sam asked.

Tom nodded. He had seen his dad do it before. "You need water. Water makes fire go away. You can use a hose or a bucket or a cup. But you have to be careful and not get burned." He said.

"Good, Tom. You are smart. Do you want to help me put out the fire?" Sam asked.

"OK, Sam. But let's watch it for a little bit more. It is so pretty." Tom said.

They sat on the grass and watched the fire. It made them feel warm and happy. They talked about their mail and their pictures and their friends. They forgot about everything else. They were dizzy from the fire. They did not see the smoke or hear the sirens. They did not know that the fire people were coming.

Tom was scared too. He dropped the scissors and ran back to the fence. But he was too late. The tiger jumped and caught him with its paw. It scratched his arm and made it bleed.

Ben and Lily looked at their mom. They felt a little bad, but they still wanted to play.

"Sorry, mom, but we are having fun. We don't want to be quiet. We want to play," they said.

Their mom sighed. She knew they were just kids, but she also needed some peace.

"Listen, kids, I know you want to play, but you have to be quiet for a little while. It's not normal to be so loud all the time. Sometimes you have to resist your urge to make noises and be respectful of others. Do you understand?" she said.

Ben and Lily nodded. They understood their mom, but they still felt bored.

"Okay, mom, we will try to be quiet. But can we play something else?" they asked.

Their mom smiled. She was glad they were willing to try.

"Sure, you can play something else. How about you play a game of I spy? You can use your eyes and your brains, but not your mouths. Do you want to try that?" she said.

Ben and Lily nodded again. They liked the game of I spy. They thought it was fun and challenging.

"Okay, mom, we will play I spy. You go first," they said.

Their mom nodded. She was happy they agreed to play a quiet game. She hoped they would enjoy it and let her finish her work.

"Okay, kids, I spy with my little eye something that is red and round and sweet. Can you guess what it is?" she said.

Ben and Lily looked around the living room. They saw many things, but they did not see anything that was red and round and sweet. They thought hard and tried to guess.

"Is it a ball?" Ben asked.

"No, it's not a ball," their mom said.

"Is it a balloon?" Lily asked.

"No, it's not a balloon," their mom said.

Ben and Lily were puzzled. They did not know what it was. They kept looking and thinking.

"Is it a...?" Ben started to say, but then he saw it. He saw what it was. He smiled and pointed.

"It's an apple!" he said.

Their mom smiled and clapped.

"Yes, it's an apple! Well done, Ben! You guessed it right!" she said.

Lily smiled and clapped too.

"Good job, Ben! You are smart!" she said.

Ben felt proud and happy. He liked the game of I spy. He liked to be quiet and use his eyes and his brains. He looked at his mom and his sister and said:

"Thank you, mom. Thank you, Lily. This is a fun game. Can I go next?" he said.

Their mom nodded and hugged him.

"Of course, you can go next, Ben. I'm proud of you for being quiet and respectful. And I'm proud of you too, Lily. You are both good kids. I love you," she said.

Ben and Lily hugged their mom back.

"We love you too, mom. You are the best," they said.

They played the game of I spy for a while. They were quiet and respectful and had fun. Their mom finished her work and joined them. They were a happy family.

Once upon a time, there was a woman who was deaf. She couldn't hear anything, not even birds singing. She lived in a small house with her cat, who belonged to her. 

One day, a little girl came to the woman's house. "Hello," said the little girl. "What's your name?" The woman couldn't hear her, so the little girl waved her hands to get her attention. "My name is Lily," she said. 

The woman smiled and waved back. "Nice to meet you, Lily," she signed. "I'm Sarah. This is my cat, Fluffy. He belongs to me." 

Lily looked at Fluffy and smiled. "He's so cute!" she said. "Can I pet him?" Sarah nodded and Lily gently stroked Fluffy's fur. "He's so soft," she said. 

From that day on, Lily visited Sarah often. They would play games and draw pictures together. Even though Sarah couldn't hear, they still had lots of fun. And Fluffy was happy to have a new friend too.

Max followed Whiskers through the woods until they came to a big, round trap.

One day, Lily and Ben saw a big truck outside their house. It was full of coal. The driver was a mean and selfish man. He did not care about anyone but himself. He said he was going to sell the coal to the rich people in the town.

Lily and Ben had an idea. They waited until the driver went inside a shop. Then they ran to the truck and took some coal. They put it in their pockets and ran back to their house. They were very happy. They thought they could make a fire and be warm.

But when they got home, they saw their mother waiting for them. She looked sad and angry. She had seen them steal the coal. She said, "Lily and Ben, what have you done? You know stealing is wrong. Tom and Anna became very scared. They did not want to stay in the basement. They wanted to go back to their mom and dad. They ran to the stairs and shouted for help.

"Mom! Dad! Help us! There is something in the basement!"

Mom and Dad heard their cries and came to the basement. They turned on the light and saw Tom and Anna. They hugged them and asked them what happened.

Tom and Anna told them about the door and the sound. Mom and Dad looked at the door and saw a small cat. It was hiding behind the door. It was the cat that made the growl.

Mom and Dad laughed and explained to Tom and Anna that the cat was not bad. It was just scared of the noise and the dark. They picked up the cat and showed it to Tom and Anna. The cat was cute and soft. It purred and licked their faces.

Tom and Anna felt silly and happy. They apologized to the cat and petted it. They asked Mom and Dad if they could keep the cat. Mom and Dad agreed and said they could name it Flash. Tom and Anna liked the name. They thanked Mom and Dad and hugged Flash. They decided to play with Flash in the basement. But this time, they left the door open and the light on.

"Uh-oh!" Tom and Lily said. They were scared.

They hugged their mom and dad. They were happy and safe. They learned a new word: dive. That's what the big duck did to eat their clay ducks.

The fish did not answer. They swam around in the water. They were happy and free.

Lily wanted to see the fish too. She climbed on the barrel next to Ben. She leaned over and peered into the water. She saw her face and the fish. She giggled and clapped her hands.

Lily wanted to catch a fish too. She reached out her hand and dipped it in the water. She felt something wet and slippery. She pulled out her hand and saw a fish. It was green and shiny. It wriggled and splashed.

"Look, Ben, I caught a fish too!" she said. "It is smooth and squishy!"

They learned a lesson. They should not play with things that do not belong to them. They should respect the lives of other creatures. They should be careful and kind.

Ben and Sam were brothers who lived on a big farm. They liked to play outside with their dog, Spot. Sometimes they helped their dad with the farm work, like feeding the chickens and milking the cows.

One day, their dad asked them to help him pass the wheat to the truck. The wheat was yellow and soft, and it grew in a big field. Ben and Sam took big baskets and filled them with wheat. Then they carried them to the truck, where their dad was waiting.

"Good job, boys!" their dad said. "You are very strong and helpful. We have almost filled the truck with wheat. We will take it to the market and sell it."

There was a little girl sitting in the middle of the wheat. She was wearing a blue dress and had long brown hair. She looked sad and lonely. She did not see Ben and Sam.

"Who is she?" Ben whispered to Sam.

"I don't know," Sam whispered back. "Maybe she is lost. Maybe she needs help."

Ben and Sam decided to talk to the girl. They walked slowly towards her, trying not to scare her. Spot followed them, wagging his tail.

"Hello," Ben said softly. "What is your name?"

The girl looked up and saw Ben and Sam. She was surprised, but not afraid. She smiled a little.

"My name is Lily," she said. "Who are you?"

"We are Ben and Sam," Sam said. "We live on this farm. This is our dog, Spot. He is very friendly."

Lily reached out and petted Spot. He licked her hand. She giggled.

"I like your dog," she said.

"Thank you," Ben said. "Why are you here? Where are your mom and dad?"

Lily's smile faded. She looked down.

"I don't have a mom and dad," she said. "I live in the orphanage. It is a big house with many children, but no one loves us. Sometimes we go out to play, but we have to be careful. It is so pretty and quiet. I wanted to stay here."

Ben and Sam felt sorry for Lily. They could not imagine living without a mom and dad, or being hit and yelled at. They wanted to help her.

"That is very sad," Ben said. "You should not be alone. You should have a family who loves you."

"Would you like to come with us?" Sam asked. "We can take you to our house. Our mom and dad are very nice. They will not hit you or yell at you. They will give you food and clothes and a bed. They will play with you and hug you. They will be your friends."

"Are you sure?" she asked. "Will they really like me? Will they let me stay?"

"Yes, we are sure," Ben and Sam said together. "They will like you. They will let you stay. They have a big heart and a big house. There is room for you. Come on, Lily. Trust us. We will be your brothers."

Tom liked to go to the lake with his dad. His dad was a fisherman. He had a big boat and a long stick with a string and a hook. He would throw the string in the water and wait for a fish to bite.

Tom wanted to be a fisherman too. He had a small boat and a short stick with a string and a hook. He would copy his dad and throw the string in the water. But he never caught any fish. He only caught weeds and rocks and cans.

One day, Tom was sad. He asked his dad why he could not catch any fish. His dad smiled and hugged him. He said, "Don't worry, Tom. You are a good fisherman. You just need some practice. And you need to remind yourself of some things."

"What things?" Tom asked.

"Well, you need to remind yourself to be patient. Fish are shy and smart. They don't always bite right away. You need to wait and watch and listen. And you need to remind yourself to be quiet. Fish can hear you if you talk or sing or shout. They get scared and swim away. And you need to remind yourself to be cool. Fish like cool water. They don't like hot water. You need to find a shady spot or a deep spot where the water is cool."

Tom nodded and thanked his dad. He said he would try to remind himself of those things. He went back to his boat and his stick and his string and his hook. He threw the string in the water and waited and watched and listened. He was quiet and cool. And soon, he felt a tug on his string. He pulled and pulled and pulled. And he caught a fish. A big fish. A cool fish.

Tom was happy. He showed his fish to his dad. His dad was proud. He said, "Well done, Tom. You are a great fisherman. You reminded yourself of the things you needed to do. And you caught a fish. A big fish. A cool fish."

Tom and his dad hugged and smiled. They put the fish in a bucket and went home. They cooked the fish and ate it for dinner. It was yummy. Tom said, "I like being a fisherman. I like the lake. I like the boat. I like the stick. I like the string. I like the hook. I like the fish. I like you, dad."

His dad said, "I like you too, Tom. You are my cool fisherman."

One day, Lily and Spot go for a walk in the park. They see many flowers and trees and birds. They also see a big pond with ducks and frogs. Lily and Spot stop by the pond to drink some water and rest.

"Hello, what is your name?" a voice says. Lily looks up and sees a boy with a red hat and a bike. He is smiling at her and Spot.

"I am Lily and this is Spot. He is my pony," Lily says.

"He is a lovely pony. Can I pet him?" the boy asks.

"Yes, you can. He is very friendly. But be gentle, please," Lily says.

The boy comes closer and strokes Spot's mane and nose. Spot nuzzles the boy and makes a soft sound. The boy laughs and says, "He likes me. Can I ride him?"

Lily thinks for a moment. She likes the boy, but she also loves Spot. She does not want to share him with anyone. But she also wants to be nice and make a new friend.

"OK, you can ride him. But only for a little while. And you have to hold on tight and be careful," Lily says.

"Thank you, Lily. You are very kind. I will be careful, I promise," the boy says.

He puts his hat on the ground and climbs on Spot's back. Lily holds Spot's reins and walks beside them. They go around the pond and see the ducks and frogs again. Tom and Lily liked to collect things. They had a big box full of shells, rocks, feathers, and stickers. One day, they went to the park with their mom. They saw a big drain near the pond. They wondered what was inside.

"Let's go see!" Tom said.

"OK!" Lily said.

They ran to the drain and looked down. They saw some water, some leaves, and some shiny things. They wanted to collect them.

"Look, a coin!" Tom said. He reached his hand into the drain.

"Be careful!" Lily said. "It's cold and wet!"

Tom felt the cold water on his fingers. He grabbed the coin and pulled it out. He smiled.

"I got it!" he said. He showed it to Lily.

"Wow!" Lily said. "Can I have one too?"

She looked into the drain again. She saw another coin. She also reached her hand into the drain.

"Ouch!" she said. She felt something sharp. She pulled her hand out. She had a cut on her finger.

"Are you OK?" Tom asked.

"It hurts!" Lily said. She started to cry.

Mom heard them and came over. She saw their hands and the drain.

"What are you doing?" she asked.

"We were collecting coins!" Tom said.

"That's not a good idea!" Mom said. "The drain is dirty and dangerous. You could get hurt or sick. Come on, let's go wash your hands and put a band-aid on your finger."

She took them to the bathroom and cleaned their hands. She put a band-aid on Lily's finger and gave her a hug.

"Next time, collect something safer, OK?" she said.

"OK, Mom," Tom and Lily said.

They learned their lesson. They decided to collect flowers instead. They picked some from the park and gave them to Mom. She smiled and thanked them.

They had a nice day at the park. They still liked to collect things, but not from the drain.

Jenny was so happy with her yummy porridge. She served it to her family and they all enjoyed it. The porridge made them feel full and happy. From that day on, Jenny loved to spin in the field and pick wheat.

Once a small bird was flying near a chimney when it saw the most beautiful flower. It was the brightest flower it had ever seen - it looked like it was made of sunshine.

The bird wanted to fly down and see the flower more closely, so it did. As soon as it touched the ground, the small bird could hear the flower singing. The flower was so pretty it almost made the bird forget it could fly.

The bird asked the flower why it was singing. The flower said it was singing because it was so happy to bloom. Then it asked the bird to listen very carefully - it was calling to a deaf bee.

The bee was busy flying from one flower to another, collecting sweet nectar to make honey. But the bee was deaf, and it couldn't hear the flower's song.

The bird knew the flower wanted a friend so badly, so it decided to help. It flew around the flower and started chirping very loudly, so the deaf bee could hear it.

The bee looked up and saw the beautiful flower. He flew to it and the flower and the bee became friends. The flower stopped singing, but it was still the most beautiful flower in the world.

The pup shivered harder than ever as the bear got closer and closer. All of a sudden, the pup heard a clip-clop sound coming from behind him. It was a horse with a big man riding on it. The man had a big, red bag and he was heading straight for the pup and the enormous bear! 

The man shouted and the bear stopped in its tracks. The pup knew he was safe! The man scooped the pup up in his bag and took him home. From then on, the pup always wore his little red collar with the silver bell. That way, if he ever got lost again, someone would hear the bell and find him!

Lily smiles and says, "Yes, I like birds. They are pretty and happy. And they have colors. They can make rainbows in the sky. I wish I could fly like a bird. Do you wish that too?"

Ben nods and says, "Yes, I wish that too. Flying would be fun. We could see many things from the sky. And we could visit other places. Maybe we could find more books like this one. And more animals to discuss."

Lily and Ben hug and say, "We are fine friends. We like to discuss things. And we like to learn new things. Books are good. And animals are good. And thumbs are good. And we are good."

The kitten drank the milk and licked its whiskers. Lily was happy that she could help the kitten. From that day on, the kitten became Lily's best friend and they played together every day.

Once upon a time, a dog named Max went for a walk with his owner, Sarah. Max wore a red collar that matched Sarah's shirt. They walked and talked about the trees, birds, and flowers they saw. Suddenly, Max saw a squirrel and ran after it with great speed. Sarah called out, "Max, come back!" but he didn't listen. 

Max chased the squirrel until he got tired and stopped. The squirrel was gone, but Max found an interesting stick to play with. Sarah caught up to him and said, "Max, you scared me! You need to listen when I call you." Max wagged his tail and licked Sarah's hand. She put the stick in her pocket and they continued their walk. 

When they got home, Sarah gave Max a treat and took off his collar. Max was happy to be home and cuddled up next to Sarah on the couch. "Today was an adventure," Sarah said, and Max barked in agreement. They both fell asleep, dreaming of their next walk together.

Lily got a really bad headache and had to go to the hospital. She learned that she needed to be patient and listen to her mom's teachings. She never made that mistake again.

"Okay, see you tomorrow," said the frog.

"Cat," Lily repeated. She smiled. She learned a new word.

They read more words together. They had fun. But they did not see a man coming. The man was crazy. He did not like children. He did not like books. He saw Lily and Ben under the tree. He got angry.

Lily and Ben were scared. They cried. They did not understand why the man was so mean. They wanted their book back.

Tommy loved yogurt. He liked to eat it every day after lunch. But today, he could not find his yogurt in the fridge. He asked his mom, "Where is my yogurt?"

Mom said, "I'm sorry, Tommy. We ran out of yogurt. But I promise I will buy some more when we go to the store later."

Tommy felt sad and anxious. He wanted his yogurt now. He did not like to wait. He said, "But I want it now, Mom. Please, please, please."

Mom said, "I know, Tommy. But we have to wait. How about we play a game while we wait? Do you want to play with your cars or your blocks?"

Tommy thought for a moment. He liked to play with his cars and his blocks. But he liked yogurt more. He said, "No, Mom. I don't want to play. I want yogurt."

Mom said, "Tommy, I understand. But you have to be patient. I promise I will get you yogurt as soon as we can. Can you trust me?"

Tommy looked at his mom. He saw that she was smiling and kind. He knew that she loved him and always kept her promises. He said, "OK, Mom. I trust you. I will wait for yogurt. But can I have a hug?"

Mom said, "Of course, Tommy. You can have a hug. And a kiss. And a high five. You are a good boy, Tommy. And I love you very much."

Tommy hugged his mom. He felt better. He said, "I love you too, Mom. And I'm sorry for being grumpy. Can we play with my cars now?"

Mom said, "Yes, Tommy. We can play with your cars now. And then we will go to the store and get some yogurt. And maybe some other treats too. How does that sound?"

Tommy said, "That sounds great, Mom. Thank you, Mom. You are the best mom ever."

Mom said, "You are welcome, Tommy. You are the best son ever."

One day, a hunter went to the forest to look for animals. He saw a big deer with horns and wanted to take it home. He had a gun that made loud noises and hurt the animals. He pointed the gun at the deer and was ready to shoot.

But then, he heard a voice behind him. It was a little girl with curly hair and a red dress. She was holding a basket of flowers and berries. She said, "Please, don't hurt the deer. He is harmless. He only eats grass and leaves. He has a family and friends. He is not yours to take."

The hunter was surprised and turned around. He saw the little girl and felt ashamed. He lowered his gun and said, "Who are you? How did you get here?"

The little girl said, "I am Lily. I live in the cottage near the forest. I come here every day to pick flowers and berries. I love the forest and the animals. They are my friends. They are not afraid of me, because I am kind and gentle. You should be kind and gentle too."

The hunter felt sorry and said, "You are right, Lily. I was wrong to try to take the deer. I don't need to hurt the animals. I have enough food and clothes at home. I will leave the forest and the animals alone. I will be kind and gentle too."

Lily smiled and said, "Thank you, hunter. You are a good person. I hope you will come back to the forest someday, but not to hunt, but to enjoy the beauty and the peace. Maybe then, the animals will be your friends too."

The hunter nodded and said, "Maybe, Lily. Maybe." He put his gun away and walked back to his car. He left the forest and the animals in peace. He never forgot Lily and her words. He learned to respect and love the forest and the animals. He became a better person.

The note said: "I made pastry for you, but don't eat them until I come back. They are very hot and you might burn your mouth. Love, mom."

Sara and Ben were restless. They wanted to eat the pastry so badly. They could smell the sweet and buttery aroma from the kitchen. They decided to search for the pastry and sneak a bite. They tiptoed to the kitchen and saw a big tray of pastry on the counter. They climbed on a chair and reached for the pastry.

"Wow, they look so yummy!" Sara said.

"Let's try one!" Ben said.

They each grabbed a pastry and took a big bite. But they soon regretted it. The pastry was so hot that it burned their tongues and lips. They screamed and dropped the pastry. They ran to the sink and tried to cool their mouths with water. But it was too late. They had blisters and sores on their mouths. They cried and cried.

Mom came back and heard their cries. She ran to the kitchen and saw the mess. She saw the note on the floor and the half-eaten pastry on the counter. She realized what had happened. She was angry and sad. She scolded Sara and Ben for disobeying her and hurting themselves. She took them to the doctor and they had to take medicine and eat soft food for a week. They missed their pastry and felt sorry for their mistake.

The moral of the story is: You should listen to your mom and not be greedy. Pastry is good, but not worth burning your mouth.

Lily and Ben were playing with their toys in the living room. They had a lot of fun making noises and pretending to be animals. Lily had a big doll that she liked to hug and dress up. Ben had a small car that he liked to zoom and crash.

"Look at my car, Lily!" Ben said. "It can go very fast and make loud sounds. Vroom, vroom, beep, beep!"

"Look at my doll, Ben!" Lily said. "She can talk and sing and dance. Hello, hello, la, la, la!"

They showed each other their toys and smiled. They liked to share and play together.

But then, something strange happened. Lily's doll started to shrink. It became smaller and smaller, until it was the size of a mouse. Lily was scared and sad. She did not know what to do.

"Ben, Ben, help me!" Lily cried. "My doll is shrinking! Where is she going?"

Ben looked at Lily's doll and saw that it was very tiny. He did not know what to do either. He wondered if his car would shrink too.

"Maybe it is a magic toy," Ben said. "Maybe it can change its size. Maybe it can grow back."

He picked up the tiny doll and held it in his hand. He tried to make it bigger by blowing on it and rubbing it. But nothing happened. The doll stayed small and quiet.

Lily and Ben were very confused and worried. They did not like this game. They wanted their toys to be normal again.

They decided to ask their mom for help. They ran to the kitchen, where their mom was making lunch. They showed her the tiny doll and told her what happened.

"Mom, mom, look!" Lily said. "My doll shrank! She is so small and empty! Why did she shrink?"

"Mom, mom, look!" Ben said. "Lily's doll shrank! She is so small and empty! How can we make her big again?"

Their mom looked at the tiny doll and was surprised. She did not know how it shrank either. She thought it was a strange toy.

"Where did you get this doll, Lily?" she asked.

"I got it from the mailman," Lily said. "He gave me a big box with a bow. He said it was a special order for me. He said it was a gift from grandma."

Their mom remembered that their grandma had called her yesterday and told her that she had sent a present for Lily. She had said it was a doll that could do amazing things. She had said it was a secret.

Their mom realized that their grandma had sent a magic doll. She smiled and hugged Lily and Ben.

"Don't worry, my loves," she said. "Your grandma loves you very much and she wanted to surprise you. This doll is not empty. She is full of magic. She can shrink and grow and do other things. She is a very special toy. You just have to learn how to play with her."

She took the tiny doll and whispered something in her ear. The doll nodded and smiled. Then, she started to grow. She became bigger and bigger, until she was the same size as before. Lily and Ben were amazed and happy. They clapped and cheered.

"Wow, mom, you are so smart!" Ben said. "You know how to make the doll big again!"

"Wow, mom, you are so kind!" Lily said. "You know how to make me happy again!"

Their mom kissed them and gave them the doll. She told them to be careful and gentle with her. She told them to say thank you to their grandma. She told them to enjoy their lunch.

Lily and Ben thanked their mom and hugged her. They thanked their grandma and hugged the doll. They enjoyed their lunch and their toy. They had a lot of fun making noises and pretending to be animals. They learned to love and share and play. They were very happy.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to visit their grandma every week. Grandma lived in a big house with a garden and many flowers. She always gave them cookies and milk and told them stories.

One day, when they went to visit grandma, they saw a new animal in the garden. It was chubby and furry and had a long tail. It was a raccoon!

"Look, Ben, a raccoon!" Lily said. "Can we pet it?"

"I don't know, Lily. Maybe it's not friendly," Ben said.

But Lily was curious and ran towards the raccoon. The raccoon saw her and hissed. It showed its sharp teeth and claws. Lily was scared and stopped.

"Go away, raccoon! You are mean!" Lily shouted.

Grandma heard the noise and came out of the house. She saw the raccoon and Lily and Ben.

"Oh, no! That's Rocky, the raccoon. He's not a pet, he's a pest. He comes to steal my food and make a mess. You should stay away from him, he's dangerous," Grandma said.

She took a broom and chased the raccoon away. Then she hugged Lily and Ben and took them inside.

"I'm sorry, Grandma. I didn't know he was bad," Lily said.

"It's okay, Lily. You didn't mean to. But you have to be careful with wild animals. They can hurt you or make you sick. Next time, just look at them from a distance and don't touch them," Grandma said.

She gave them cookies and milk and told them a story about a brave princess and a friendly dragon. Lily and Ben forgot about the raccoon and enjoyed their visit. They learned a lesson and had fun.

"We are Lily and Tom. We are playing. Who are you?" Lily said.

"I am Gus. I am a ghost. I like to play too. Can I join you?" Gus said.

Lily and Tom looked at each other. They did not know what to do. They had never met a ghost before.

"Are you nice?" Tom asked.

"Yes, I am nice. I do not hurt anyone. I just want to have fun. Please let me play with you." Gus said.

Lily and Tom thought for a moment. They decided to give Gus a chance. They were wise. They knew that not all ghosts were bad.

"Okay, you can play with us. But you have to balance on the log too. It is our game." Lily said.

"Okay, I will try. But I do not have feet. I have to float." Gus said.

He floated to the log and tried to balance on it. He wobbled and swayed. He almost fell off. Lily and Tom laughed. They helped him stay on the log. They taught him how to balance. Gus was happy. He made new friends. They played until it was dark. Then they said goodbye and went home. They promised to meet again. They had a lot of fun.

"Thanks, I like it too," said Johnny. "Do you want to play a game?"

"Sure, what game?" asked Lily.

"Let's tie our shoelaces together and try to run around the ranch without falling over," said Johnny.

Lily thought it sounded like a fun game, so they tied their shoelaces together and started running. It was hard to balance, but they laughed and had a good time. When they were done, they sat down and ate some oranges that Johnny's mom had picked from the trees on the ranch.

"That was a fun game," said Lily. "Thanks for playing with me."

"Anytime, Lily," said Johnny. "I like playing with you."

After they finished making the soup, they sat down to eat. Lily felt very sleepy after eating the warm soup. She said to her mommy, "Mommy, I feel so sleepy. Can we take a nap together?" Her mommy hugged her and said, "Yes, Lily. Let's take a nap and dream about all the fun things we can do together on a sunny day."

The moral of the story is that even on a yucky day, you can still have fun and make memories with the people you love.

Once upon a time, there was a mole in the garden. He was very small and had a long nose. He loved to dig in the dirt and eat plant roots.

One day, the mole was digging in the dirt. Suddenly, he heard a loud noise. He was very surprised! He looked up and saw a bird in a tree. The bird was making loud noises with its beak.

The mole was very scared. He quickly ran away and hid behind a rock. But even from behind the rock, he could still hear the loud noises from the bird. He was too scared to come out of his hiding place.

Suddenly, he heard another loud noise - this one was different. He was so surprised that he forgot to be scared! He looked up and saw a lady in the garden. She was laughing and clapping her hands. The mole had never seen a lady before!

He slowly came out from behind the rock. The lady was very kind and smiled at the mole. She gave him a big hug. The mole felt so loved and happy! He knew that he would never forget his surprise visitor.

John was so happy that he could carry this light and it was so reliable. He promised himself he would always take good care of the light. Everywhere he goes, he takes the light with him and tells everyone how reliable it is.

Every morning Mary liked to stand in front of her crystal and rub her fingers over it. It made her feel so calm and happy. 
Mary couldn't help but smile whenever she saw the crystal, it was just so beautiful.
One day Mary's sister came over to play. She wanted to have a go of rubbing the crystal. Mary was happy to share her special crystal but warned her sister not to drop it. 
But as her sister was rubbing the crystal, it suddenly slipped out of her hands and landed on the ground. It made a terrible noise when it hit the floor and suddenly started to crack.
Mary was so sad and she started to cry. Why did her crystal have to break? 
But when she looked a little closer, she saw that it wasn't broken at all. The crystal was still the same sparkly, clear crystal it used to be! 
So Mary was able to smile again, and she was so happy that she could rub her crystal one more time.

Suddenly, he noticed smoke! It was coming from his house! Timmy ran as fast as he could, but it was too late - his house was on fire. 

The fire was too big and too strong. Firefighters hurried to put it out, but the flames were burning everything. Timmy was so sad to see his modern house ruined. 

But then something amazing happened. The firefighters used the limes from Timmy's basket to douse the flames! They rubbed the limes on the burnt walls, and soon the fire was completely put out. Everyone was so happy!

Timmy learned a lesson that day: sometimes even things that seem small and weak, like limes, can help save the day.

The dragon let out a big roar, which stopped the frog from jumping. The frog closed his eyes and trembled in fear. But then, something very strange happened. The big dragon started to laugh. He said to the frog, "Come here and don't be scared. I won't hurt you."

The frog hopped closer and soon realized the dragon wasn't so scary after all. The frog asked, "What are you doing out here?" The dragon replied, "I'm out exploring the fog. It's really fun!"

The frog was happy his fear had vanished, so he decided to hop along with the dragon. Together they explored the foggy field and made a new friend. The frog and dragon laughed and played until the sun went down and then said goodbye. The fat frog hopped away, making sure to always remember the dragon in the fog.

He was so happy. All the other vegetables were so excited to see the pretty little radish and they cheered and clapped when they saw him.

Once upon a time, there was a pink potato. It wanted to march forward, but it was stuck in one spot. It saw a big, black bird fly above its head and thought to itself, "If only I could fly like that bird, I could march anywhere I wanted."

The pink potato was so determined to march that it thought hard and long about how to fly. Finally, it figured out a way. It lifted up its stem and began to flap it back and forth. It was working! 

The pink potato kept on flapping until the stem became too heavy and it fell back to the ground. It didn't give up though. It had a plan. It rolled down a hill, and as it did, it kept on flapping its stem. The wind caught it and lifted it up and carried it farther and farther away.

Now, the pink potato is free to march all around. It floats in the sky and marches from flower to flower, all the while waving goodbye with its stem.

The End.

Moral of the story: Always be careful when buying things, to make sure it is not a fake sale.

When it was time to go home, Emma didn't want to give the ball to anyone. Lily suggested they play a game where they would take turns holding the ball. Emma liked that idea and agreed. They had so much fun playing together and taking turns.

As they were leaving, Lily said goodbye to Emma and closed the gate to the park. She felt happy that they had worked out a way to play with the ball together.

"Wow, look at that!" Lily said. "Let's try it!"

They ran to the wheel and took turns to turn it. They had fun spinning and laughing. But then, a grumpy boy came and pushed them away.

"That's mine!" he shouted. "Go away!"

Lily and Ben were sad and scared. They did not want to fight with the grumpy boy. They wanted to share the toy.

"Please, can we play with you?" Lily asked. "We can take turns."

The grumpy boy shook his head. "No, it's mine! I don't want to share!"

He turned the wheel faster and faster. He did not care if Lily and Ben were hurt.

Lily and Ben did not know what to do. They looked around and saw a nice lady who worked in the park. She saw what was happening and came to help.

"Hello, children," she said. "What's the matter?"

She listened to Lily and Ben and the grumpy boy. She smiled and said, "I have an idea. Why don't we all play together? We can make a game. We can skip to the wheel, turn it, and then skip away. The one who skips the fastest wins. Does that sound fun?"

Lily and Ben nodded. They liked the game. They hoped the grumpy boy would like it too.

The grumpy boy thought for a moment. He did not want to be alone. He wanted to have fun. He nodded too.

"Okay, let's play," he said.

The nice lady clapped her hands. "Great! Let's start!"

They all skipped to the wheel, turned it, and skipped away. They laughed and cheered. They made friends. They had fun.

I will be a good friend."

The moral of the story is: Be nice to others and do not be proud. God loves you and hears your prayers. He will help you when you are in trouble, but he also wants you to learn from your mistakes.

"Look, Sam, I can do this one!" Lisa said, pointing to a picture of a girl standing on one leg and holding the other one behind her head. "It is called king pigeon pose. Can you do it?"

Sam shook his head. He did not think he could bend his leg like that. He tried to copy Lisa, but he lost his balance and fell on the floor. He hurt his knee and it started to bleed. He felt a sharp pain and a warm wetness on his skin.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Sam cried. He was scared and sad. He wanted to go home.

Lisa felt bad for Sam. She did not mean to make him fall. She wanted to make him happy, not hurt. She was embarrassed. She thought Sam would think she was silly and mean.

"I'm sorry, Sam, I'm sorry!" Lisa said. She ran to get a band-aid and some water. She helped Sam clean his wound and put the band-aid on. She gave him a hug and a kiss.

"It's okay, Lisa, it's okay," Sam said. He felt better. He saw that Lisa was sorry and kind. He did not think she was silly or mean. He smiled and hugged her back.

"Thank you, Lisa, thank you," Sam said. "You are a good friend. And you are very flexible. Maybe you can teach me some easier poses next time."

Lisa nodded. She was happy. She and Sam were still friends. They decided to play with her dolls instead of doing yoga. They had fun and laughed. They forgot about the fall and the blood. They were happy.

Ben felt sad. He thought his trumpet was better than her ball. He said, "But my trumpet is loud and funny. It can make any sound I want. It's more fun than your ball."

The girl shook her head and said, "No, it's not. Your trumpet is noisy and annoying. It can only make one sound at a time. It's not fun at all."

Ben got angry. He said, "Yes, it is. My trumpet is the best. You don't know anything about music. You're silly and boring."

He blew his trumpet as hard as he could, hoping to make her change her mind. But instead of making her like his trumpet, he made her cry. She dropped her ball and ran away, sobbing.

Ben's mom saw what happened and came to him. She was not happy. She said, "Ben, what did you do? Why did you make that girl cry? That was not nice at all."

Ben felt ashamed. He said, "I'm sorry, mom. I just wanted to play with her. I wanted to show her my trumpet. I thought she would like it."

His mom said, "Ben, you can't force people to like what you like. Everyone has different tastes and preferences. You have to respect that. You have to be kind and polite to others. You have to use your trumpet to make people happy, not sad."

Ben nodded. He said, "I understand, mom. I was wrong. I should have asked her if she wanted to play with me, not with my trumpet. I should have listened to her, not shouted at her. I should have used my trumpet to make friends, not enemies."

His mom smiled and hugged him. She said, "That's right, Ben. I'm glad you learned your lesson. Now, why don't you go and apologize to that girl? Maybe you can still play with her, if she wants to. Maybe you can share your trumpet and her ball. Maybe you can find something in common. Maybe you can have fun together."

One day, they wanted to sleep in the tent at night. They asked their mom if they could. She said no, it was too cold and dark outside. They asked their dad. He said maybe, if they were good and ate their dinner and brushed their teeth.

Tom and Lily were very excited. They ate their dinner very fast and brushed their teeth very well. They put on their pajamas and their warm hats and their flashlights. They said good night to their mom and dad and ran to the tent.

But when they got to the tent, they saw something scary. There was a big shadow inside the tent. It looked like a monster with big teeth and claws. They heard a loud growl. They were very afraid. They dropped their flashlights and ran back to the house.

They knocked on the door and cried for their mom and dad. Their mom and dad opened the door and hugged them. They asked them what was wrong. Tom and Lily told them about the monster in the tent. Their mom and dad looked at each other and smiled.

They took them to the tent and showed them what was inside. It was not a monster. It was their dog, Rex. He had sneaked into the tent and made himself comfortable. He was snoring and wagging his tail. He was happy to see them.

Tom and Lily felt silly and relieved. They laughed and petted Rex. They decided to let him sleep in the tent with them. They got their flashlights and their blankets and cuddled with Rex. Their mom and dad said good night and went back to the house.

They permitted them to sleep in the tent, but they told them to be careful and not to make too much noise. They said they would check on them in the morning. Tom and Lily said thank you and they loved them. They closed the tent and turned off their flashlights. They fell asleep with Rex, dreaming of adventures.

Ben and Lily were friends. They liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a person with a big bag of candy. The candy looked yummy. Ben and Lily wanted some.

"Hello, person. Can we have some candy?" Ben asked.

"Sure, kids. You can have some candy. But you have to do something for me first. You have to change your clothes with me," the person said.

"Why?" Lily asked.

"Because I like your clothes. They are pretty and colorful. And mine are old and dirty. Come on, it's a fair trade. Candy for clothes," the person said.

Ben and Lily thought about it. They really wanted the candy. They decided to change their clothes with the person. They took off their clothes and gave them to the person. The person gave them the candy and put on their clothes.

"Thank you, kids. Enjoy your candy. Bye-bye," the person said. He ran away with their clothes.

Ben and Lily ate the candy. It was yummy. But then they felt sick. Their stomachs hurt. They wanted to go home. But they had no clothes. They were cold and ashamed. They cried.

"Help! Help! We need help!" they shouted.

But no one heard them. No one came to help them. They were alone and sad. They wished they never changed their clothes with the person. They wished they never ate the candy. They learned a hard lesson. The end.

Tim and Kim are twins. They like to play with toys and books. One day, they find a big book with many pictures. The book is about animals and plants. They open the book and see many things.

"Look, Kim, this is a cell," Tim says. He points to a small circle with dots and lines. "It is very small. You need a glass to see it."

"What is a cell?" Kim asks. She looks at the circle. "Is it an animal or a plant?"

"A cell is a part of an animal or a plant," Tim says. He remembers what Mom told him. "All animals and plants are made of many cells. They are very hard to see."

Kim nods. She turns the page and sees a big picture of a lion. The lion has a mane and teeth. It looks scary.

"Wow, this is a lion," Kim says. She points to the picture. "It is very big. You need a cage to keep it."

"What is a cage?" Tim asks. He looks at the picture. "Is it a house or a toy?"

"A cage is a thing with bars and a door," Kim says. She remembers what Dad showed her. "Some people keep animals in cages. They are very hard to open."

Tim shakes his head. He does not like cages. He thinks animals should be free.

"I do not like cages," Tim says. "They are not nice. I like cells. They are interesting."

Kim smiles. She likes cells too. They are fun to learn.

"I like cells too," Kim says. "They are cool. Let's see more cells."

They turn the page and see more pictures of cells. They learn many things. They have fun with the big book.

"Please, horse, please!" Tom said. "We want to play with you! You are our friend!"

But the horse shook its head and neighed. It walked away to the shade of a big tree. It lay down on the grass and closed its eyes.

Lily was sad. She loved the horse very much. She wanted to make it happy. She had an idea. She ran to the house and got a bucket of water and a sponge. She came back to the horse and said, "Horse, I have a surprise for you! I want to help you cool down!"

She poured some water on the sponge and rubbed it gently on the horse's back. The horse opened its eyes and felt the water. It was cold and nice. It made the horse feel better. It lifted its head and licked Lily's cheek. It thanked her with a soft nicker.

Tom saw what Lily did and smiled. He got another bucket of water and a sponge and joined her. They both washed the horse and made it wet and shiny. The horse enjoyed their attention and care. It stood up and trotted to them. It invited them to climb on its back. It was ready to play again.

Tom and Lily were happy. They hugged the horse and thanked it for being their friend. They rode on the horse and had fun. They did not mention the hot sun anymore. They only felt the breeze and the joy. They loved the horse and the horse loved them. They were a happy family.

"Where is the other raven?" she asked Ben.

Ben smiled. He had the other raven card in his hand. He wanted to win the game. He was about to put the card on the table, when he heard a loud caw outside the window.

He turned his head and saw a real raven sitting on a branch. The raven looked at him with shiny eyes. Ben thought the raven was very cool. He forgot about the game and ran to the window.

"Look, Lily, a real raven!" he shouted.

Lily saw the raven too. She also thought it was cool, but she remembered the game. She saw the raven card in Ben's hand. She quickly grabbed it and put it with her own raven card.

"I found the other raven!" she said. "I win the game!"

Ben came back from the window. He saw that Lily had taken his card. He felt sad. He had lost the game.

"That's not fair!" he said. "You took my card!"

Lily laughed. She thought Ben was silly. She gave him a hug.

"It's just a game, Ben," she said. "Don't be sad. The raven is still there. Maybe he wants to play with us too."

They looked at the window again. The raven was still there. He cawed again, as if he agreed. Lily and Ben smiled. They decided to play another game with the raven. They had fun. They forgot who won or lost. They were happy.

"Hey, give me back my car!" Ben shouted. He ran to the sofa and tried to get his car. But the car was broken. One of the wheels had come off. Ben started to cry.

"Look what you did, Lily! You broke my car! It was my favorite car!"

Lily felt sorry. She did not mean to break Ben's car. She just wanted him to be quiet. She hugged Ben and said, "I'm sorry, Ben. I did not want to break your car. I was just mad at you. Can we share your car and my doll?"

Ben stopped crying. He looked at Lily and said, "OK, Lily. We can share. But you have to be nice to my car. It is still a good car."

Lily and Ben smiled. They fixed the car with some tape and played with it and the doll. They learned to share and not ignore each other.

Baa is a sheep who likes to grow wool. He thinks his wool is powerful. It keeps him warm and soft. He likes to show his wool to the other sheep. They say his wool is nice, but not powerful.

One day, a man comes to the farm. He has a big bag and a sharp thing. He looks at the sheep. He points at Baa. He says, "I want that one. He has the most wool."

Baa is scared. He does not want to go with the man. He does not want to lose his wool. He runs away. He hides behind a tree. He hopes the man will not find him.

But the man is clever. He sees Baa's wool behind the tree. He walks to the tree. He grabs Baa. He says, "You can't hide from me. Your wool is too big and bright. I will take your wool and make a sweater."

Baa cries. He says, "Please, no. My wool is powerful. It is part of me. It is my friend. Please, let me keep my wool."

The man laughs. He says, "Your wool is not powerful. It is just wool. It is mine now. You don't need it. You will grow more wool soon."

He puts Baa in his bag. He takes his sharp thing. He cuts off Baa's wool. He throws the wool in another bag. He leaves Baa in the bag. He goes away.

Baa feels cold and sad. He misses his wool. He thinks his wool was powerful. He thinks he was wrong. He thinks he is nothing without his wool. He wishes he could have his wool back. He wishes he could be powerful again.

Lily and Tom were having a picnic with their mom and dad. They had sandwiches, apples, cookies, and jelly. Lily loved jelly. She liked how it was sweet and wobbly and shiny. She wanted to eat all the jelly by herself.

"Can I have some jelly, please?" Tom asked Lily.

"No, it's mine!" Lily said. She held the jar of jelly close to her chest. "You can have a cookie."

"But I want jelly too," Tom said. He felt sad. He liked jelly as well. He thought it was fun to poke and squish and spread.

Mom and dad saw Lily and Tom. They did not like how Lily was being selfish. They wanted to teach her to share and to value her brother.

"Lily, why don't you give some jelly to Tom?" mom asked. "He is your brother and he is hungry. You have plenty of jelly. Sharing is nice."

"But I love jelly!" Lily said. "It's my favorite. I don't want to share."

Dad took the jar of jelly from Lily. He opened it and showed her. "Look, Lily, this jelly is very thick. It is too much for one person. If you eat it all, you will get a tummy ache. And you will make Tom unhappy. Do you want that?"

Lily looked at the jar of jelly. She saw how thick it was. She also looked at Tom. He had tears in his eyes. She felt sorry for him. She realized that she was being mean. She shook her head.

"No, I don't want that," she said. "I'm sorry, Tom. Here, you can have some jelly. I will share with you."

She took a spoon and scooped some jelly for Tom. She gave it to him with a smile. Tom smiled back. He thanked her and took a bite. He said it was yummy.

Mom and dad were proud of Lily. They hugged her and told her she was a good sister. They also gave her a cookie. Lily felt happy. She learned that sharing and valuing her brother was better than keeping all the jelly for herself.
